allPatterns.platform: Wix ProGallery / Wix Pro Gallery & Slideshow image blocks
allPatterns.name: Filename-as-alt-text on auto-imported gallery images
allPatterns.description: When a user drags images into a Wix gallery/slideshow without filling the optional alt field, the rendered gets either an empty/absent alt or the raw upload filename echoed into a title/alt-like attribute, so informative product/portfolio images announce as 'IMG_4821' or 'DSC0093-2-1024x768' or nothing at all. The alt field is optional in the editor and routinely skipped.
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: An alt attribute IS present and non-empty, so axe/Lighthouse 'image-alt' passes. Only a human reading the page can tell that 'IMG_4821~mv2.jpg' is a meaningless filename rather than a description of what the image conveys, and whether the image is informative (needs real alt) or decorative (needs alt="").
allPatterns.realWorldNote: WebAIM 2025 Million found 55.5% of pages have alt-text problems; Wix support docs make the gallery alt field optional, and Wix accessibility guides repeatedly flag ProGallery/Slideshow images as the most common missing/inadequate-alt source. https://support.wix.com/en/article/accessibility-preparing-your-images-and-galleries

allPatterns.platform: Squarespace blog / Summary block grid
allPatterns.name: Triple-redundant 'Read More →' links sharing one destination
allPatterns.description: Each summary item auto-emits the thumbnail image, the post title, AND a 'Read More →' link, all three pointing to the same post URL. Screen-reader users tabbing the link list hear 'Read More, link / Read More, link / Read More, link' with no way to distinguish posts, and the same destination is reachable three times. The 'Read More →' text cannot be edited or removed through built-in settings.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup: Spring Tips Read More →
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Each <a> has non-empty text ('Read More →'), so link-name checks pass; the redundancy/ambiguity is only a problem when the links are read out of context as a list, which requires human judgment about whether the link purpose is determinable. Tools can't know the three links go to the same place is intended vs. confusing.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Amy Carney's hands-on Squarespace audit: 'Redundant links: image, heading, and Read More all link to same destination' and the Read More link cannot be customized or unlinked. https://theamycarney.com/2024/04/02/observations-on-squarespace-accessibility/

allPatterns.platform: Squarespace blog/collection pages (multiple themes)
allPatterns.name: Multiple H1s — one per article title on a listing page
allPatterns.description: Squarespace blog index and collection pages output the site/page title as an H1 and then render EACH article title in the feed as its own H1, producing many H1s on one page. Screen-reader users navigating by heading level get a flat, ambiguous outline with no single page topic and no h2-level grouping of the list.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup:
Journal

First Post

Second Post
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Multiple H1s are technically valid HTML5 and most automated rules only warn (or not at all) about it; whether the heading hierarchy actually communicates the page's structure is a semantic judgment. axe flags 'page-has-heading-one' as satisfied, not violated.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Amy Carney's Squarespace audit: 'Multiple H1 headings on single page (one per article title) despite page already having H1.' https://theamycarney.com/2024/04/02/observations-on-squarespace-accessibility/

allPatterns.platform: Wix Editor (absolute-positioned canvas layout)
allPatterns.name: DOM/reading order diverges from visual order on overlapping layouts
allPatterns.description: Wix's drag-anywhere canvas positions elements absolutely; the algorithm that derives DOM order from on-screen coordinates can mis-order overlapping, stacked, or strip-based sections, so keyboard Tab order and screen-reader reading order jump around (e.g., footer CTA before main content, a caption before its image, a price before the product name).
allPatterns.typicalMarkup:
Add to cart
Handmade Mug — $24
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Automated tools generally cannot determine the 'correct' meaningful sequence — they don't know the visually-intended reading order, so they can't tell that DOM order contradicts it. Detecting the mismatch requires a human comparing the visual layout to the tab/reading order.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Wix Engineering describes building an algorithm to make DOM order reflect visual position precisely because the canvas otherwise breaks navigation order; Wix support has a dedicated 'Checking and Adjusting a Site's DOM Order' article. https://www.wix.engineering/post/the-story-of-making-wix-accessible

allPatterns.platform: Squarespace Form Block (AJAX same-page submit)
allPatterns.name: Success/confirmation message injected without a live region
allPatterns.description: On submit, the form swaps in a visible 'Thank you, your message has been sent' confirmation in place of the form, but the inserted node is not a role=status / aria-live region and focus is not moved to it. Sighted users see success; screen-reader users hear nothing and may believe the submission failed and re-submit.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup: Thank you! Your message has been sent.
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: The message is valid visible text in the DOM; a static scan sees correct markup and no error. Catching it requires dynamically submitting the form AND observing (with AT or by checking for a live region / focus move) that the status change is never announced — a behavioral, human-in-the-loop check.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Amy Carney's Squarespace audit: 'Same-page confirmation messages don't alert screen reader users of state changes' and 'error lists aren't linked to inputs or focused.' https://theamycarney.com/2024/04/02/observations-on-squarespace-accessibility/

allPatterns.platform: Squarespace search block (instant/predictive results)
allPatterns.name: Instant search results render with no announcement or result count
allPatterns.description: Results appear on each keystroke beneath the search box, but the results container is not a live region and the result count is never announced, so screen-reader users don't know results appeared, how many, or that the list changed. The Quick Preview is also keyboard-inaccessible and the spinner is silent.
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Static analysis finds a labeled search input and valid result links. The absence of an announcement is a dynamic behavior that only surfaces when you type and listen with a screen reader; tools can't infer that the live update should have been announced.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Amy Carney's Squarespace audit: 'Search results appear on keystroke but screen readers aren't notified of appearance or result count; processing spinner lacks announcements; Quick Preview not keyboard accessible.' https://theamycarney.com/2024/04/02/observations-on-squarespace-accessibility/

allPatterns.platform: Squarespace mobile navigation (hamburger toggle)
allPatterns.name: Menu toggle button with no aria-expanded and no text label
allPatterns.description: The default mobile nav is a burger icon button that opens/closes an overlay menu but never exposes its expanded/collapsed state (no aria-expanded) and offers no visible/accessible text label, so it announces only as 'button' and its open/closed state is invisible to AT.
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: axe will flag a button with NO accessible name, but it will NOT flag a missing aria-expanded state on a custom toggle (state correctness is contextual). Determining that this particular button is a disclosure that should report its state, and that its name is unclear, needs human inspection of behavior.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Amy Carney's Squarespace audit: navigation menu button 'missing aria-expanded or equivalent' and 'no visible text label option (e.g., Menu).' https://theamycarney.com/2024/04/02/observations-on-squarespace-accessibility/

allPatterns.platform: Wix custom 'box'/container used as a clickable button (div with role/handler)
allPatterns.name: Visible button label differs from auto-applied accessible name
allPatterns.description: Designers build buttons from Wix container boxes with a click action plus an auto/template aria-label, while a text element inside shows different wording. The result: visible text says 'Get Started' but the accessible name is 'Site Button' or 'Button1' (a generated component name), so SR output, the page's visual label, and voice-control targets disagree.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup: Get Started
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: The element HAS a role and a non-empty accessible name, so name/role checks pass. axe's label-content-name-mismatch rule only fires in narrow cases and can miss div-based controls; deciding that 'Site Button' fails to describe a 'Get Started' control and mismatches the visible text needs a human reading both.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Wix Engineering notes developers 'mimic a native element rather than use the semantic element,' needing tabindex fallbacks; community threads cover adding aria-label to Wix buttons/links, and Deque's label-content-name-mismatch rule documents this class. https://www.wix.engineering/post/the-story-of-making-wix-accessible

allPatterns.platform: Carrd single-page sites (default sections / overlay text)
allPatterns.name: Low-opacity white text fails contrast while looking 'designed'
allPatterns.description: Carrd templates frequently set body/caption text in semi-transparent white (rgba(255,255,255,0.3) or 0.15) over photographic or gradient backgrounds. It reads as a tasteful muted style to the designer but falls far below 4.5:1, and over a varying photo background the effective ratio changes per region.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup: Subscribe for updates
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Automated contrast tools can't reliably compute the ratio of text over a CSS background-image/photo (no solid color to sample) and often skip or guess; the rgba opacity composited against an image is exactly the case scanners punt on, leaving a human to sample the rendered pixels.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Audit of a Carrd site found 50 automated issues incl. text using rgba(255,255,255,0.3) and rgba(255,255,255,0.15) weakening contrast. https://dev.to/yuridevat/accessibility-check-2-195p

allPatterns.platform: Wix templates (default theme text styles)
allPatterns.name: Light-gray body/caption text below 4.5:1 in the default palette
allPatterns.description: Many Wix templates ship with light-gray secondary text (captions, subtitles, footer text, form helper text) that fails AA contrast out of the box. Because it's the template default, it propagates everywhere the user adds that text style without them realizing it's non-compliant.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup: Crafted with care since 2014
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: This one IS reliably caught by axe/Lighthouse when text sits on a solid color — included for completeness. The judgment-light cases (solid background, real text node) are auto-detectable; only the over-image variants need a human.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Wix ADA guides repeatedly cite 'many Wix templates use light gray text that fails contrast requirements' as a default-template problem. https://accessibe.com/blog/knowledgebase/wix-website-accessibility

allPatterns.platform: Wix Slideshow / Pro Gallery slider & lightbox; Wix popups
allPatterns.name: Carousel/slider/lightbox not keyboard operable or focus-trapping
allPatterns.description: Wix sliders and popups frequently can't be advanced/controlled by keyboard, and opened lightboxes/popups either don't move focus in, leave focus on the page behind, or trap it without an Esc exit. Arrow controls are mouse-only; the auto-rotating slideshow can't be paused.
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Whether a control is reachable AND operable by keyboard, whether focus moves into a dialog, and whether Esc escapes are runtime/interaction facts. Static scans see divs/images; they can't exercise Tab/Enter/Esc to discover the inoperability or the trap.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Wix ADA guides: 'Wix sliders are frequently keyboard inaccessible' and 'Wix popups often fail keyboard navigation.' https://www.lowcodewebsite.com/post/wix-accessibility-complete-guide-to-fix-issues-achieve-ada-compliance-2026

allPatterns.platform: Wix sites (focus-indicator suppression / 'blue boxes off')
allPatterns.name: Visible focus indicator disabled by default for aesthetics
allPatterns.description: Wix historically disabled the visual focus ring ('blue boxes') by default because designers felt it 'doesn't look good,' and the editor still exposes a toggle to turn focus indicators on/off. With them off, keyboard users have no idea where focus is across links, buttons, and gallery items.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup:
a:focus, button:focus { outline: none; box-shadow: none; }
/* template default suppressing the focus ring */
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Automated tools rarely detect a MISSING focus indicator — outline:none is legal CSS and a custom indicator might exist via box-shadow or a class. Confirming there is no perceptible focus indicator on real focus requires tabbing through and watching, a visual human check.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Wix Engineering: 'the visual focus was actively disabled up until now... the reason was a design one - the focus indication doesn’t look good.' Wix support has a 'turning the blue boxes on and off' article. https://www.wix.engineering/post/the-story-of-making-wix-accessible

allPatterns.platform: Squarespace 404 / system pages
allPatterns.name: System page reuses generic title and has no H1
allPatterns.description: The default 404 page (and some system pages) ships with no option for an H1 and inherits a non-unique page title, so AT users who land there get a page with no main heading and a <title> that doesn't say it's a 'Page Not Found' page, leaving them disoriented about where they are.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup:
<title>My Studio</title>
<main><!-- 404 copy but no <h1> --></main>
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: A <title> is present and non-empty, so 'document-title' passes; whether it actually describes THIS page (vs. being the generic site title repeated) is a semantic comparison a human must make. A missing h1 is at most a warning, not a hard failure, in most scanners.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Amy Carney's Squarespace audit: 404 page has 'no H1 heading option available' and is 'missing a unique page title.' https://theamycarney.com/2024/04/02/observations-on-squarespace-accessibility/

allPatterns.platform: Squarespace image-caption overlay (dark-overlay style) & gallery captions
allPatterns.name: Caption text over a dark-overlay/photo overlay fails contrast
allPatterns.description: The built-in 'dark overlay' caption style puts light caption text over a semi-transparent dark scrim on top of a photo. On bright or busy images the scrim isn't enough and the foreground/background ratio drops below 4.5:1 in some regions of the image while passing in others.
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Text over a translucent scrim over a photo has no single computable background color; scanners cannot evaluate per-pixel contrast across the image and typically skip it, so a human must visually sample worst-case regions.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Amy Carney's Squarespace audit: 'Dark overlay option produces poor foreground/background color contrast' for image captions. https://theamycarney.com/2024/04/02/observations-on-squarespace-accessibility/

allPatterns.platform: Squarespace / Wix gallery & multi-item blocks
allPatterns.name: Visual lists of items not exposed as semantic lists
allPatterns.description: Galleries, summary grids, and icon rows render as a pile of sibling divs/anchors rather than <ul><li>, so screen-reader users never hear 'list, 12 items' and lose the count and grouping that sighted users get from the visual grid.
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Divs are valid markup and there's no rule that says 'these siblings should be a list' — recognizing that a visual grid conveys a list relationship that the markup fails to express is a semantic/visual judgment automated tools cannot make.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Amy Carney's Squarespace audit: 'Image galleries not auto-generated as semantic lists.' https://theamycarney.com/2024/04/02/observations-on-squarespace-accessibility/

allPatterns.platform: Squarespace / Wix contact & booking forms (custom-styled fields)
allPatterns.name: Placeholder used as the only label; errors not programmatically tied to fields
allPatterns.description: Custom-styled form fields rely on the placeholder as the visible label (no <label>), so the field's name vanishes once the user types, and error messages are shown as text near the form rather than associated with the offending input (no aria-describedby, no aria-invalid, no focus to the error).
allPatterns.typicalMarkup: Please enter a valid email.
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: axe can catch an input with NO accessible name, but a placeholder often supplies a name so the input 'passes'; that the label disappears on input and that the visible error isn't programmatically linked to its field are judgment/behavioral checks. Whether helper text constitutes adequate instructions is semantic.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Wix accessibility guides warn that Wix Forms/Bookings with custom field styling can leave 'labels and error messages not programmatically associated'; Amy Carney found Squarespace form errors not linked to inputs or focused. https://accessibe.com/blog/knowledgebase/wix-website-accessibility

allPatterns.platform: WordPress Media Library / auto-alt plugins (Auto Image Alt Text from Filename, Image Attributes Pro) on any Twenty* or builder theme
allPatterns.name: Alt text is the raw filename (or template default 'image')
allPatterns.description: WordPress core never auto-populates the alt attribute, so editors either leave it blank or install a plugin that copies the filename into alt. The img then carries semantically useless alt like 'IMG_4521', 'DSC00231-1024x683', 'hero-banner-final-v2' or a slug like 'untitled-1'. It passes the 'has alt' check but conveys nothing; informative images get garbage and decorative images get noise.
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: axe/WAVE/Lighthouse only check that alt is present and non-empty; a filename string satisfies that. Deciding whether alt actually describes the image's purpose, or whether the image is decorative and should have empty alt, requires looking at the image and the surrounding context.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: WordPress core does not set alt from anything; WPBeginner and the 'Auto Image Attributes From Filename' plugin (200k+ installs) explicitly populate alt from the filename. https://wordpress.org/plugins/auto-image-attributes-from-filename-with-bulk-updater/ and https://brutalbusiness.com/automatically-set-the-wordpress-image-title-alt-text-other-meta/

allPatterns.platform: Gutenberg / page-builder post grids, blog templates, ACF loops (Elementor Posts widget, Divi Blog module)
allPatterns.name: Repeated 'Read More' / 'Learn More' links with no in-context distinction
allPatterns.description: Post-loop templates render an identical generic call-to-action link for every post in the grid. A screen-reader user pulling up the links list hears 'Read more, Read more, Read more...' (or 'Learn more') with nothing to distinguish destinations. Builders default this string and rarely add per-post screen-reader-text.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup:
Our 2024 Annual Report

Lorem ipsum...

Read More

Spring Sale Details

Lorem ipsum...

Read More
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: The links have non-empty, programmatically-determinable accessible names, so 4.1.2 passes. Judging that 'Read More' is non-descriptive out of context, and that ten of them are ambiguous, requires understanding the link text means nothing without the adjacent heading.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: WordPress accessibility handbook documents the screen-reader-text fix precisely because 'read more'/'click here' are 'unintelligible out of context.' https://make.wordpress.org/accessibility/handbook/markup/the-css-class-screen-reader-text/ and https://equalizedigital.com (Accessibility Checker flags this pattern)

allPatterns.platform: Elementor Icon Box / Icon List widget (Font Awesome icon fonts)
allPatterns.name: Icon-only link/button whose accessible name is the icon glyph or empty
allPatterns.description: Icon Box and social-icon widgets render a link wrapping only a Font Awesome <i> with no text. The accessible name comes out empty (empty link) or, when the icon font exposes a glyph/private-use character, a screen reader announces a meaningless symbol name. CSS pseudo-element icons (::before content) can be read aloud as random characters bearing no relation to the visible icon.
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: When the accessible name is truly empty, axe catches it (link has no discernible text). But when the icon font leaks a glyph name or a pseudo-element character into the name, the link is technically 'named' and tools pass it while the announced name ('private-use-F07A') is meaningless — judging that requires hearing what's announced vs. seeing the cart icon.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Elementor docs and abrightclearweb note Icon widgets 'create empty links and adjacent identical links'; Divi review notes CSS pseudo-element icons cause screen readers to 'announce the symbol's name, which has no semantic relationship.' https://www.abrightclearweb.com/elementor-accessibility/ and https://elevagedigital.com/improving-wordpress-divi-accessibility/

allPatterns.platform: Divi Contact Form module / Elementor Form widget with placeholder-only fields
allPatterns.name: Form field labeled only by placeholder (or label visually hidden by default)
allPatterns.description: Divi's Contact Form hides labels by default and relies on placeholder text; Elementor forms are frequently configured the same way. The input has no <label>/aria-label, only a placeholder, so once the user types the label vanishes and screen readers may announce the field as unlabeled. Required-field asterisks are color-only with no text alternative.
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: This one is largely linter-catchable: axe flags inputs with no programmatic label. It is included for completeness, though confirming the placeholder text is the only labeling and that the asterisk's meaning is color-only still benefits from human review.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Divi review: 'The Divi Contact Form module hides labels by default, making it difficult for screen readers to interpret form inputs.' https://reciteme.com/us/news/divi-accessibility/

allPatterns.platform: Divi theme defaults / Elementor global button styles / many premium themes
allPatterns.name: Focus outline removed globally via CSS (outline:none / :focus reset)
allPatterns.description: Theme stylesheets ship 'outline:0' on a, button, and form controls (or :focus { outline:none } for visual polish) and never add a replacement focus style. Keyboard-only users lose all indication of focus position across links, menu items, and buttons. Sometimes :focus has a style but :focus-visible / actual tab traversal shows nothing on builder-generated buttons.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup:
a, button, input, .et_pb_button { outline: none; }
button:focus { outline: 0; box-shadow: none; }
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Automated tools cannot reliably detect a missing focus indicator: outline:none is legal if a visible alternative (border/box-shadow/background change) exists. Determining there is NO perceivable focus change requires tabbing through and visually observing each interactive element across states.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Divi reviews repeatedly cite removed focus indicators: 'The CSS in the Divi theme has removed visible focus indicators.' https://elevagedigital.com/improving-wordpress-divi-accessibility/ and divi-accessibility plugin 'adds a visual outline to focusable elements.' https://github.com/campuspress/divi-accessibility

allPatterns.platform: Elementor / Divi mega-menu and dropdown nav (default Nav Menu widget, Max Mega Menu)
allPatterns.name: Submenu opens on hover only, not keyboard-operable, not dismissible (1.4.13)
allPatterns.description: The dropdown/mega-menu reveals on mouse hover via CSS :hover. Tab key skips the submenu entirely (submenus stay display:none for keyboard), and even where they appear they cannot be dismissed with Esc and aren't hoverable/persistent. Keyboard and screen-reader users cannot reach second-level items, and the hover-revealed panel fails Content on Hover or Focus.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup:
• Products
    • Item A
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Static scanners see valid nested lists and links and report no error. Discovering that the submenu only opens on hover, that Tab never reaches it, and that Esc does not dismiss the hover panel requires actually operating the menu by keyboard and mouse.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Divi 'dropdown menus can only be activated with a mouse... submenus remain hidden.' https://arrowdesign.ie/fix-divi-menu-accessibility-issues-wcag-compliance-solution/ ; WP Trac #49950 'submenu should be dismissible' (1.4.13); https://216digital.com/how-to-make-mega-menus-more-accessible/

allPatterns.platform: Elementor Accordion / Toggle widget, Divi Toggle/Accordion module
allPatterns.name: Custom accordion header not keyboard-operable / wrong tabindex / missing aria-expanded
allPatterns.description: Accordion headers are <div>/<a href="#"> with a jQuery click handler. The clickable element either isn't focusable, or has the wrong tabindex (Elementor puts tabindex on the wrong child so the control is invisible to keyboard), and Enter/Space don't toggle because the handler only listens for click. aria-expanded is missing or, in some builder versions, slapped onto a <summary> where it is invalid.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup:
Section One
...
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: role=tab with no working keyboard handler can look structurally fine to a scanner; some tools flag missing aria-expanded but not the click-only handler. Confirming Enter/Space actually toggle the panel, and that focus lands and the expanded state is announced, requires keyboard testing.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Elementor issue #23335 'Accordion and Toggle have broken accessibility'; #11246 'aria-expanded not used'; community: 'JQuery click event handler cannot be triggered via keypress.' https://github.com/elementor/elementor/issues/23335 and https://testpros.com/accessibility/making-elementor-essential-addons-accordion-accessible/

allPatterns.platform: Elementor Image Carousel / Slides widget, Divi Slider, Smart Slider 3
allPatterns.name: Auto-advancing carousel: icon-only controls + slide content/links hidden from AT
allPatterns.description: Slider widgets auto-rotate with no clearly labeled pause/stop control. Prev/next arrows are icon-only with empty accessible names; pagination dots are unlabeled buttons. Off-screen slides are not consistently hidden from the accessibility tree, so screen-reader users encounter duplicate/moving content and links to slides they can't see.
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Empty arrow/dot names are partially catchable, but judging that hidden slides leak focusable links into the tab order, and that there is no labeled pause control, requires observing the running carousel and its focus behavior across slide states.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Elementor audit: 'Images in the carousel advance automatically every three seconds with no mechanism for pausing, stopping, or hiding.' https://www.accessibilitychecker.org/blog/elementor-website-accessibility/

allPatterns.platform: Gutenberg blocks / page-builder sections used as visual styling (Heading block, Divi Text module set to H-tag)
allPatterns.name: Heading levels chosen for font size — skipped levels and visual-only headings
allPatterns.description:
Editors pick heading tags by how big they look. A section header is set to H4 because H2 'looks too big', producing H1 then H4 with no H2/H3. Conversely, bold styled text that visually functions as a heading is left as a

, so the document outline has no entry. Builders make every text element's tag a free-form dropdown, so structure tracks visual size, not meaning.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup:
Welcome

Our Services

Pricing
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss:
Tools can flag a skipped level (H1->H4) but cannot decide that styled bold

SHOULD be a heading, nor whether a heading is descriptive of the section it labels. That mapping of visual prominence and meaning to correct level/semantics is human judgment.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Learn WordPress and WP handbook warn against using headings for visual styling / skipping levels. https://learn.wordpress.org/tutorial/using-headings-for-accessibility-and-seo/ ; Gutenberg document outline only warns, doesn't enforce.

allPatterns.platform: Elementor Form widget / Divi Contact Form / WPForms — submission feedback
allPatterns.name: Success/error toast not in a live region; errors flagged by color only
allPatterns.description: After AJAX form submit, the success or error message is injected into a <div> that is not a live region and not focused, so screen readers never announce it. Inline validation marks invalid fields with a red border/red text only, with no programmatic error association and no text describing what's wrong or how to fix it.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup: Your message was sent!
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: The success div is valid HTML; nothing in the static DOM signals it should announce on change. Detecting that a dynamically-inserted status isn't announced requires triggering the submit and observing AT silence. Color-only error indication also needs visual judgment that no text/icon backs the red.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: ARIA live-region guidance: 'create an empty element and then update its content' — builder messages don't. https://a11y-blog.dev/en/articles/aria-live-regions/ ; matches harness 4.1.3 / 3.3.x shadow lanes.

allPatterns.platform: Divi / Elementor button modules with icons and 'global' default labels (Pricing Table, CTA)
allPatterns.name: Multiple buttons with identical generic accessible name ('Get Started', 'Submit')
allPatterns.description: Pricing-table and CTA modules ship every plan's button reading the same default ('Get Started' / 'Buy Now' / 'Learn More'). Out of context the buttons are indistinguishable by name, so a screen-reader user navigating buttons can't tell the Basic from the Pro plan. Editors leave the default because per-button custom labels 'look kludgy.'
allPatterns.typicalMarkup:
Basic

...Get Started

Pro

...Get Started

Enterprise

...Get Started
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Each button has a valid, non-empty name, so 4.1.2 passes and there's no duplicate-id type error. Recognizing the three 'Get Started' names are ambiguous and need to encode the plan requires understanding the page's meaning and the navigate-by-button workflow.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Beaver Builder review: Pricing Table 'buttons all say the same thing – Get Started, and while you could edit this... it would make the buttons look kludgy.' https://wpshout.com/beaver-builder-accessibility/

allPatterns.platform: WordPress theme demo import / starter templates (Astra, OceanWP, Elementor Kits, Divi Layouts)
allPatterns.name: Placeholder demo content left in production — default title, lorem ipsum, stock alt
allPatterns.description: One-click demo imports populate the site with template defaults that editors forget to replace: the page <title> stays 'My WordPress Site' / 'Just another WordPress site' tagline, headings and links read 'Lorem ipsum dolor', CTA buttons say 'Button Text', and stock images carry the kit's generic alt. Titles don't uniquely describe the page; link text is meaningless Latin.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup:
Lorem Ipsum Dolor

Click Here
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: A <title> of 'Just another WordPress site' is present and non-empty (2.4.2 passes a presence check); lorem-ipsum link text is non-empty. Recognizing the content is unreplaced placeholder that fails to describe topic/purpose is a semantic judgment a linter can't make.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Demo/starter imports use lorem ipsum and template defaults; WPBeginner documents importing dummy content; 'Just another WordPress site' is the stock tagline. https://www.wpbeginner.com/wp-themes/how-to-add-dummy-content-for-theme-development-in-wordpress/

allPatterns.platform: WooCommerce / Elementor product loop on Storefront, Astra, Divi shops
allPatterns.name: Color/variant swatches conveyed by color only; 'Add to cart' names not unique
allPatterns.description: Product variation swatches are colored squares/links with no text or accessible name ('Red', 'Blue' is visual-only), so the choice is unperceivable without color. In the shop grid every product's 'Add to cart' / 'Select options' button has the same name, indistinguishable by product when navigating by button.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup: Add to cart
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Color-only meaning (1.4.1) is not statically detectable — a tool can't know the red square MEANS 'red' with no text backup. Repeated 'Add to cart' names are valid names. Both require understanding what the visual conveys and the by-button navigation experience.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: WooCommerce color-swatch plugins render color-only links; equalizedigital and WebAIM repeatedly flag color-only controls and duplicate 'add to cart' button names as a top WordPress-shop barrier. https://equalizedigital.com/accessibility-checker/

allPatterns.platform: Elementor Tabs widget / Beaver Builder Tabs / Divi Tabs module
allPatterns.name: Tab panel content not associated/announced; div tabs missing roles
allPatterns.description: Builder 'tabs' render as styled divs. Either the tablist/tab/tabpanel roles and aria-controls/aria-selected are absent (so it's just clickable divs), or the roles exist but the panel content isn't reliably exposed when a tab is activated. Selecting a tab by keyboard may not move focus or announce the newly revealed panel.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup:
• Description
  • Reviews
...
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Plain divs with click handlers raise no role/value error in a scanner (nothing claims to be a tab). Where roles do exist, confirming the active panel's content is actually announced on switch needs screen-reader testing, not static analysis.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Beaver Builder review: with tabs 'the content of an expanded tab isn't reliably read out.' https://wpshout.com/beaver-builder-accessibility/

allPatterns.platform: Divi / Elementor on mobile — fixed-width builder sections and reflow
allPatterns.name: Fixed-pixel-width sections break reflow at 320px / 400% zoom
allPatterns.description: Builder sections built with fixed pixel widths / absolute positioning / large negative margins cause horizontal scrolling or content loss at 320 CSS px (or 400% zoom). Low-vision users get a two-direction-scroll layout instead of a single reflowed column. Often paired with a viewport meta that suppresses zoom.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup: ...
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Reflow / horizontal-scroll-at-400% is not assertable from static markup — a tool can't compute the rendered layout at the target viewport. Confirming content is lost or requires two-axis scrolling needs visual checking at 320px / 400% zoom.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Divi review: viewport meta blocks zoom and fixed-width sections hamper reflow. https://elevagedigital.com/improving-wordpress-divi-accessibility/

allPatterns.platform: Twenty* core themes & most premium/builder themes — landmark structure
allPatterns.name: Ambiguous duplicate nav landmarks and structure built from role-less divs
allPatterns.description: Builder sections wrap everything in generic <div>s with no landmark roles, so the page has no programmatic structure beyond the theme header/footer. Where multiple <nav> regions exist (primary menu, footer menu, breadcrumbs) they share no distinguishing aria-label, so a screen-reader user hears 'navigation, navigation, navigation' with no way to tell them apart.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup:
...primary menu...
...footer menu...
...
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Duplicate unlabeled nav landmarks may or may not be flagged depending on the tool, and missing landmark structure built from divs isn't an error per se. Judging that two 'navigation' regions are ambiguous and that the page lacks a sensible landmark map needs human review of how it's announced.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Builder pages are notorious for div-soup with no landmarks; Divi historically shipped no skip link and weak landmark labeling. https://www.accessgo.de/en/divi-accessibility-overview-requirements-solutions-and-practical-examples/

allPatterns.platform: Elementor / Divi 'div as button' CTA blocks, animated counters, hotspot widgets
allPatterns.name: Div with onClick acting as a button — wrong/absent role, no keyboard, name mismatch
allPatterns.description: A styled <div> (or <a href="#">) carries a JS click handler and visually reads as a button. It exposes no button role, isn't in the tab order, and Enter/Space don't activate it. Where an aria-label is added it can mismatch the visible label (e.g. visible 'Start your free trial', aria-label left as a generic 'button' from a template), so the accessible name doesn't contain the visible text.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup: Start your free trial
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: A div with onClick and no role is invisible to the accessibility tree, so some scanners simply don't see a control to test. Detecting the visible-vs-accessible name mismatch and that it should be a keyboard-operable button requires comparing what's seen to what's announced.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Elementor #25128: aria-label custom attribute doesn't reach the <a>, producing name mismatches; div-button anti-pattern is endemic to builder CTA modules. https://github.com/elementor/elementor/issues/25128

allPatterns.platform: Shopify Dawn theme — product variant picker (color)
allPatterns.name: Color-only variant swatches with no text alternative
allPatterns.description: Color variant options render as colored circles/squares (radio inputs visually replaced by background-color chips). The only way to know which color is which is to see the chip; the accessible name is often the hex/handle or absent, so a screen reader announces 'option 1, option 2' or just the color value, and there is no non-color cue distinguishing selected vs available swatches. Color is the sole means of conveying the choice.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup: Color
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: The radio inputs are technically labeled (the <label for> exists and the value attribute carries the color name), so axe/Lighthouse see a valid, named form control and pass it. They cannot perceive that the swatch communicates the choice purely through a CSS background-color, nor judge whether the visible chip and the accessible name actually correspond, nor whether selection state has a non-color indicator.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Shopify Dawn ships swatches as color chips and merchants add color-only swatches via tutorials (made4uo.com swatch guide; Dawn issue #3112 on color swatches). Audits of Dawn flag color contrast and ARIA on swatches. https://github.com/Shopify/dawn/issues/3112 ; https://testparty.ai/blog/shopify-dawn-theme-accessibility

allPatterns.platform: Shopify / generic theme — sale price markup on product card and PDP
allPatterns.name: Sale price reads as two bare numbers with no Was/Now context
allPatterns.description: On-sale prices show the original price with a CSS strikethrough next to the discounted price. The strikethrough is purely visual; screen readers announce something like '$50.00 $30.00' with no indication which is the regular price and which is the sale price, and no 'Was/Now' or 'Sale' context. Visually-hidden context spans are missing.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup: $50.00 $30.00
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Both prices are present as real text, so there is no missing-alt or empty-element violation to flag. The <s> element conveys 'no longer accurate' semantically to almost no screen reader by default, but tools don't treat its absence of announcement as an error. Deciding that the output '$50 $30' is confusing and needs 'Was/Now' wording requires understanding the sale semantics — a human contextual judgment.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Well documented by AccessiCart ('Accessible sale prices') and the Shopify partners blog 'Developing Shopify Themes with Accessibility in Mind'; fix is visually-hidden 'Was'/'Now' spans. https://accessicart.com/accessible-sale-prices/ ; https://a11y.tips/blog/discounted-price/

allPatterns.platform: Shopify / WooCommerce — Add to Cart confirmation & cart drawer
allPatterns.name: Silent add-to-cart: drawer/toast update not in a live region
allPatterns.description: Clicking 'Add to cart' updates a cart-count bubble and slides open a cart drawer or shows a toast, but the success message is injected into a normal <div> with no role=status / aria-live. Sighted users see the confirmation; screen reader users get no announcement that the item was added, and focus is not moved into the drawer either.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup:
Item added to your cart

View cart (1)
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: The notification element is valid HTML with valid contrast and a labeled link, so static scanners pass it. The failure only manifests on interaction (clicking add-to-cart) and depends on whether the dynamically-shown node is in a live region AND whether focus is managed — a runtime behavior automated DOM scans don't simulate, and judging the right remediation (announce vs. move focus) is contextual.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: TestParty 'Beyond Alt Text' lists 'silent cart updates — screen reader users receive no confirmation' as a top hidden Shopify barrier; WooCommerce filed its own 4.1.3 fix for the added-to-cart message. https://testparty.ai/blog/beyond-alt-text-hidden-shopify-accessibility-barriers

allPatterns.platform: WooCommerce — store notices on page load (waitlist / coupon / stock)
allPatterns.name: Page-load notice not programmatically a status message
allPatterns.description: WooCommerce renders informational notices (e.g. 'To join the waitlist, click Notify me', coupon applied, 'only 2 left') as a styled div shown when the page renders. The notice has no role=status/alert and focus is not placed on it, so on a fresh page load it is visible but never announced to screen reader users.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup: To join the waitlist, please click the "Notify me" button.
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: There is no markup defect: contrast is fine and the text exists in the DOM. Whether a given message is a 'status message' that must be announced (vs. ordinary body copy) is a semantic judgment about its purpose and timing; axe/Lighthouse cannot infer intent and do not flag missing role=status on plain divs.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Filed directly against WooCommerce core as a WCAG 4.1.3 failure: 'message is visually displayed, but screen readers do not announce it because it has not been programmatically defined as a status message, and focus is not set on the message when the page loads.' https://github.com/woocommerce/woocommerce/issues/59383

allPatterns.platform: Shopify / BigCommerce — quick-view modal (Add to cart from grid)
allPatterns.name: Quick-view modal keyboard trap / no focus return
allPatterns.description: Quick-view modals open over the product grid. Two common failures: (a) focus stays on the underlying page so keyboard users tab through background content behind the overlay, or (b) focus enters the modal but Escape doesn't close it and Tab can cycle but never escape, and on close focus is not returned to the triggering 'Quick view' button — keyboard users are stranded or lose their place.
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: role=dialog may be present so structural checks pass. The trap, the missing Escape handler, and the failure to restore focus to the trigger are dynamic, interaction-time behaviors that require actually tabbing through the open modal and closing it — automated DOM snapshots don't exercise focus flow or key handlers.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: TestParty's Shopify checkout/keyboard guides explicitly call out 'quick-view modals that trap focus so keyboard users cannot escape' and modals that 'capture focus and never give it back'. https://testparty.ai/blog/shopify-checkout-keyboard-navigation-fixes ; https://testparty.ai/blog/modal-dialog-accessibility

allPatterns.platform: Shopify / WooCommerce — bulk-uploaded product images
allPatterns.name: Alt text is the filename or a generic default
allPatterns.description: Product images imported via CSV/feed or drag-drop bulk upload inherit alt text equal to the filename (e.g. 'IMG_4823' or 'product-1_2048x.jpg') or a templated default like 'Product image' / the store name. The image is informational (shows the actual product) but the alt conveys nothing about color, style, or what is shown.
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: An alt attribute is present and non-empty, which is exactly what axe/WAVE check for — so it passes 'images have alt text'. Recognizing that 'DSC_0234_2048x' or 'Product image' is meaningless and fails to describe the actual product requires reading the alt against the visible image: a semantic/visual human judgment of quality, not presence.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Baymard found 55% of ecommerce sites don't communicate informational image content via alt; WCAG.com and Siteimprove note auto/bulk imports default to filenames; AI alt-text apps exist precisely because the default is filename/blank. https://baymard.com/blog/informational-image-accessibility

allPatterns.platform: Magento Luma / third-party review widgets — star ratings
allPatterns.name: Star rating rendered with CSS width %, no text alternative
allPatterns.description: Average rating shows as filled/empty stars implemented as a background-image bar with inline width (e.g. width:80%). There is no aria-label or visually-hidden text, so screen readers announce nothing, or announce a raw '80%' with no unit, instead of 'Rated 4 out of 5 stars'. Same in third-party Shopify review apps.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup: Rating:
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: There is no to require alt on — the stars are CSS background images, which automated scanners ignore entirely. A title='80%' may exist but tools won't judge that '80%' is meaningless as a rating. Determining that this visual is conveying a 4-of-5 rating that needs a textual equivalent is a human contextual/visual judgment.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Magento Luma uses CSS-width rating bars; TestParty's Shopify barriers list cites third-party 'review widgets with star ratings without text alternatives'. https://testparty.ai/blog/beyond-alt-text-hidden-shopify-accessibility-barriers

allPatterns.platform: Shopify / WooCommerce — AJAX filter / faceted search sidebar
allPatterns.name: Facet filtering updates grid silently; no result-count announcement
allPatterns.description: Selecting a filter checkbox (size, color, price) re-renders the product grid via AJAX with no page reload. The new result count ('24 products') and any 'No results' state are not in a live region, so screen reader users don't know the grid changed or how many products remain. Some themes also replace native checkboxes with styled divs that lose keyboard operability.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup: 24 products
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: On the initial static snapshot the markup is valid (labeled checkboxes, a count div). The defect appears only when a filter fires and content swaps without an announcement — a runtime behavior. Whether the count and no-results state qualify as status messages requiring aria-live is an intent-based judgment scanners can't make.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Equalize Digital's FacetWP audit and Scott O'Hara's 'dynamic results' guidance cover exactly this; accessibility-test.org documents ecommerce faceted-search live-region gaps. https://equalizedigital.com/testing-facetwp-for-accessibility/ ; https://accessibility-test.org/blog/compliance/accessibility-for-e-commerce-product-filtering-and-faceted-search/

allPatterns.platform: Wix Stores / headless React storefronts — icon-only controls
allPatterns.name: div/span 'button' with visual label mismatching its accessible name
allPatterns.description: Cart, wishlist, quick-add and quantity controls are built as <div> or <span> with click handlers and an icon. Either there is no accessible name at all, or an aria-label was copy-pasted/templated so it mismatches the visible glyph or tooltip (e.g. a heart icon labeled 'button', or a '+' quantity stepper whose aria-label says 'Decrease'). The visible text/icon and the programmatic name disagree.
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: A linter flags the second case (clickable span with no name / no role / no keyboard handler) — that part is auto-detectable. But the first case has a role, tabindex, and an aria-label, so axe passes it; detecting that the label 'Decrease' contradicts the visible '+' glyph requires reading the icon and comparing it to the name — a visual/semantic human judgment (the 'accessible name contains visible label' check needs human eyes on the icon).
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Wix guidance notes 'missing or inappropriately applied ARIA labels' as a critical screen-reader issue and that some elements need manual fixing; TestParty lists wishlist/quick-add 'icon-only buttons without labels'. https://accessibe.com/blog/knowledgebase/wix-website-accessibility ; https://testparty.ai/blog/beyond-alt-text-hidden-shopify-accessibility-barriers

allPatterns.platform: Headless / Hydrogen / React+SPA storefronts (Shopify, BigCommerce)
allPatterns.name: <title> and H1 never update on client-side route change
allPatterns.description: Navigating from collection to product to cart happens client-side; the document <title> stays at the homepage/store name on every route, and focus is not moved to the new page's H1. Screen reader users hear the same title on every 'page' and get no signal that navigation occurred.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup:
<head><title>Acme Store</title></head>
<!-- after client-side nav to /products/blue-shirt the title is still "Acme Store";
     no React Helmet update, no focus moved to the product <h1> -->
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: A single-page audit finds a non-empty <title> and passes 2.4.2. The failure is that the title doesn't CHANGE across virtual route transitions and is identical/non-descriptive for each view — a multi-state behavior. Tools scan one DOM state and have no concept of route changes, so they never compare titles across navigations.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Widely documented SPA failure (Hidde Blog, Kitty Giraudel, Helsinki a11y model): SPAs keep a static <title> unless JS updates it on every route change. https://hidde.blog/accessible-page-titles-in-a-single-page-app/ ; https://saavutettavuusmalli.hel.fi/en/saavutettavuus-palvelukehityksessa/toteutus-ja-ohjelmistotestaus/single-page-applications-spas-notes-on-accessibility/

allPatterns.platform: WooCommerce / Magento — checkout form validation
allPatterns.name: Field errors shown as red text only, not associated with the input
allPatterns.description: On checkout submit, invalid fields turn red and a message like 'This field is required' appears, but the message is a sibling div not linked via aria-describedby/aria-errormessage, the input has no aria-invalid, and color is the only cue marking which fields failed. Screen reader users tabbing the form don't hear which fields are in error or why.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup: This field is required.
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: The error text exists and the label is associated, so structural scanners pass. They cannot verify at runtime that submitting produced an error that is (a) tied to the right field programmatically and (b) not communicated by red color alone. Confirming the association and that the message is meaningful requires submitting the form and inspecting the error/field relationship — a human/runtime judgment.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Generic but rampant in ecommerce checkout; DigitalA11y and AccessiCart describe exactly this 3.3.1 pattern (red-only, unassociated errors) and call it out for checkout flows. https://accessicart.com/wcag-level-a-sc-3-3-1-error-identification/ ; https://www.digitala11y.com/understanding-sc-3-3-1-error-identification/

allPatterns.platform: Shopify Dawn / generic themes — promo and 'Learn more' CTAs from CMS blocks
allPatterns.name: Repeated non-descriptive link text ('Shop now' / 'Learn more')
allPatterns.description: Theme content blocks and collection cards generate multiple links whose text is the same generic phrase ('Shop now', 'Learn more', 'View details') with the actual destination only conveyed by an adjacent heading or image. A screen reader user listing links hears 'Shop now, Shop now, Learn more, Learn more' with no way to tell them apart.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup:
Summer Linen Collection

Shop now

Winter Knitwear

Shop now
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Each link has visible, non-empty text and a valid href, so it passes the auto 'link has discernible text' check. Tools rarely flag duplicated generic link text, and even when they do they cannot judge whether the surrounding heading/context makes the purpose clear — determining ambiguity requires reading the link relative to its context, a human semantic judgment.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Common Dawn/theme CMS pattern; flagged in Shopify WCAG checklists (link clarity must be reviewed manually) and Wix's note that 'reviewing link clarity' is not automatable. https://easyappsecom.com/guides/shopify-wcag-compliance-checklist ; https://www.allaccessible.org/blog/shopify-accessibility-implementation-guide

allPatterns.platform: Shopify Dawn / Debut — sale badges and disabled/sold-out states
allPatterns.name: Insufficient contrast on sale badges and disabled buttons
allPatterns.description: 'Sale' / 'Sold out' badges and disabled 'Add to cart' buttons use light or theme-accent colors (e.g. light pink on white, grey-on-grey) that fall below 4.5:1 for the text, and the badge's non-text boundary can fall below 3:1. Common in default and lightly-customized Dawn/Debut palettes.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup: Sale
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: This is largely auto-detectable: axe/Lighthouse compute text contrast ratios and flag <4.5:1. Edge cases tools may miss are disabled-control text (some scanners skip disabled elements) and badge text over gradient/image backgrounds, but the core is a measurable ratio, so humanJudgmentNeeded is false.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Dawn audits specifically flag 'color contrast failures on sale badges and disabled elements' and multiple elements failing AA contrast. https://testparty.ai/blog/shopify-dawn-theme-accessibility

allPatterns.platform: Shopify / WooCommerce themes — focus styling removed on interactive controls
allPatterns.name: Focus outline suppressed on swatches, buttons and links
allPatterns.description: Themes (or merchant CSS tweaks) apply outline:none / :focus{outline:0} to buttons, variant swatch labels, and links to 'clean up' the design, leaving no visible focus indicator. Keyboard users cannot tell which swatch/button is focused while navigating the product form.
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Partly auto-detectable — some tools flag outline:none in CSS — but they cannot reliably confirm there is no adequate replacement indicator (a box-shadow or border swap may suffice) without observing the focused state. Reliable confirmation is by tabbing and watching; still, the core 'no visible focus' is verifiable, so flagged humanJudgmentNeeded=false with the caveat that replacement-indicator adequacy may need a look.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Dawn/Shopify keyboard audits repeatedly cite suppressed/weak focus indicators; TestParty and Shopify theme best-practices emphasize visible focus on all interactive controls. https://testparty.ai/blog/shopify-checkout-keyboard-navigation-fixes

allPatterns.platform: Generic ecommerce — required-field marking on cart/checkout/newsletter forms
allPatterns.name: Required fields indicated by red asterisk/color only
allPatterns.description: Checkout, account, and newsletter signup forms mark required inputs with a red asterisk styled purely via color (no 'required' word, no required/aria-required attribute, asterisk not in the label text). Users who don't perceive the color, or screen reader users, don't learn the field is mandatory until submission fails.
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: The label is associated and present, so the form passes label checks. Whether 'required' is conveyed by more than color, whether the asterisk's meaning is explained, and whether aria-required is set are partly structural but partly contextual — tools don't flag a red asterisk as a use-of-color failure because they can't tie the color to the 'required' meaning. Recognizing the instruction is missing needs human review.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: TestParty 'Beyond Alt Text' lists 'red asterisks only marking required fields without text labels' as a Shopify use-of-color (1.4.1) barrier. https://testparty.ai/blog/beyond-alt-text-hidden-shopify-accessibility-barriers

allPatterns.platform: Webflow div with Interaction (IX2) used as a button/CTA
allPatterns.name: Clickable div CTA with no role and no accessible name
allPatterns.description: Designers wire a Webflow click Interaction onto a plain Div Block (often containing only an icon or a background image), so the rendered element is a clickable div with no button/link role, not in the tab order, and no accessible name. It looks and behaves like a button visually but is invisible/inoperable to keyboard and screen-reader users.
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: A bare <div> with a click handler attached via a data-w-id Interaction has no role, no tabindex, and frequently no text — automated scanners do not flag a generic div as a 'control' because nothing in the static DOM declares it interactive; they cannot tell it carries a JS click handler that makes it a de-facto button. Recognizing it as a missing-name control requires a human to see it renders/behaves as a CTA.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Webflow's own accessibility guidance warns that click triggers should be placed on button elements rather than divs, and that role=button on a div still loses platform behaviors like spacebar activation. See Webflow accessibility checklist / 'The Webflow Way' accessibility docs: https://webflow.com/accessibility/checklist and community guidance at https://www.gracefulwebstudio.com/blog-articles/webflow-video-lightbox-accessibility-and-focus-management

allPatterns.platform: Webflow CMS dynamic image / multi-image field
allPatterns.name: CMS-bound images ship with empty or filename alt at scale
allPatterns.description: Static images can get alt text in the Designer, but CMS Collection images default to empty alt unless the author explicitly binds an alt field, and multi-image (gallery) fields ALWAYS render alt="". Editors rarely populate a dedicated alt field, so dozens of meaningful content images (product photos, team headshots, article heroes) publish with empty or auto-filename alt across every collection-list and template page.
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: alt="" is VALID markup (correct for decorative images), so a linter cannot know a CMS hero photo is meaningful content that needs a description rather than a deliberately-decorative image. When alt is the filename, axe/WAVE treat it as 'has alt' and pass it — judging that 'product-7f3a91' or 'team_photo_final_v2' is useless requires a human to compare the text to the actual image.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Finsweet/SAYU SEO guides document that Webflow CMS and multi-image fields default to empty alt and require manual field binding, and Webflow's own audit panel only inspects static images, not dynamic CMS images: https://finsweet.com/seo/article/cms-image-dynamic-alt-tags and https://help.webflow.com/hc/en-us/articles/33961330170643-Include-alt-text-on-images

allPatterns.platform: Webflow native Slider component
allPatterns.name: Off-screen carousel slides keep focusable controls and links
allPatterns.description: Webflow's Slider hides non-active slides with CSS transforms/opacity (not display:none), so links, buttons, and form fields inside the off-screen slides remain in the tab order. Keyboard users tab into invisible content, focus disappears off-screen, and the slide-dot/arrow controls are often unlabeled icon buttons.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup: Shop now
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: The off-screen slide is still visible to the accessibility tree (no display:none / aria-hidden), so scanners see normal in-DOM links and report nothing wrong; detecting that focus visually 'leaves the screen' onto a translated-off slide requires running the keyboard sequence and watching where the focus ring goes — a dynamic, visual check tools don't perform.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Accessibility guidance for sliders specifies off-screen slides must be hidden via display:none/visibility:hidden or aria-hidden + tabindex=-1, which Webflow's default Slider does not do: https://dev.to/jasonwebb/how-to-build-a-more-accessible-carousel-or-slider-35lp and https://www.flowradar.com/answer/fix-issue-slider-webflow-not-accessible-screen-readers

allPatterns.platform: Webflow native Lightbox component
allPatterns.name: Lightbox opens without focus trap, dialog role, or labeled close
allPatterns.description: Webflow's built-in Lightbox opens an overlay but does not trap focus (Tab leaves the modal to the page behind it), has no role=dialog / aria-modal, no accessible name on the dialog, and the close 'X' is an unlabeled icon. Esc behavior and focus return to the trigger are not handled.
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: A missing focus trap is a behavioral property: nothing in the static markup is 'invalid', so axe/Lighthouse cannot detect that Tab escapes the open overlay. The unlabeled close MIGHT be flagged, but confirming the dialog lacks a name and that focus returns to the trigger requires opening it and operating it by keyboard.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Documented that the Webflow lightbox lacks a focus trap (users can tab out), is missing a descriptive accessible name on the dialog, and needs custom code/ARIA to fix: https://www.gracefulwebstudio.com/blog-articles/webflow-video-lightbox-accessibility-and-focus-management and Webflow's own checklist task 'Ensure modals are keyboard navigable': https://webflow.com/accessibility/checklist/task/ensure-modals-are-keyboard-navigable

allPatterns.platform: Webflow / Framer absolute-positioned layout (CSS grid-area, position:absolute, flex order)
allPatterns.name: Visual order diverges from DOM/tab order in free-canvas layouts
allPatterns.description: On a free design canvas, authors drag elements into a visual arrangement while the DOM source order stays whatever was authored. Absolute positioning, CSS order, and grid placement make the reading/tab order jump around — e.g., a CTA visually at top-left is last in the DOM, or a sidebar reads before the main column for a screen reader.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup:
Primary CTA
Legal footnote
Headline
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Both the DOM order and the CSS are individually valid; determining that the resulting tab/reading order is 'illogical' relative to the visual layout requires a human to compare what they SEE to the order focus actually moves — automated tools have no model of the intended visual narrative.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Webflow's checklist 'Ensure focus order is logical' explicitly warns that arranging elements with CSS instead of the Navigator yields nonlinear/illogical focus order; WCAG technique C27 covers DOM-vs-visual order: https://webflow.com/accessibility/checklist/task/ensure-focus-order-is-logical and https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG20-TECHS/C27.html

allPatterns.platform: Framer (and other React SPA exporters: Typedream, Readymag)
allPatterns.name: SPA route change leaves <title> stale and focus unmoved
allPatterns.description: Page-to-page navigation is client-side. The document <title> is not updated on route change, focus stays on the clicked link (or resets to <body>), and there is no route-change announcement. Screen-reader users get no signal a new page loaded and the title still reads the landing page.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup: Pricing
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: A single-page snapshot has a valid, non-empty <title>, so a page-load scan passes 2.4.2. The defect only appears across an in-app navigation: the scanner would need to click through routes and re-check title + focus + live announcement, which static and single-load automated tools don't do.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Well-documented SPA failure: screen readers announce titles only on full page load and don't monitor title changes, and focus must be moved on route change — directly applicable to Framer/React-exported sites: https://medium.com/design-bootcamp/accessible-by-design-part-2-your-spa-single-page-application-is-broken-for-screen-readers-739769110ce1 and https://a11y-guidelines.orange.com/en/articles/single-page-app/

allPatterns.platform: Framer auto-generated headings / text layers
allPatterns.name: Heading hierarchy from visual size: skipped levels and multiple H1s
allPatterns.description: Designers style text layers by visual size and Framer lets each text layer be tagged H1–H6 (or left as a paragraph/div). The result is non-sequential heading levels (H1 → H4), several H1s on one page, decorative big text marked as a heading, or real section headings left as plain styled divs.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup:
Acme

Build faster

Features

Pricing
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Skipped levels and multiple H1s are partly linter-detectable, but the high-value errors are semantic: deciding that a big styled <div> SHOULD be a heading, or that an <h4> is functioning as the section title, requires understanding the page's meaning and visual structure — automated checks can't infer intended document outline.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: AudioEye's Framer review stresses that simply tagging headings isn't enough and that missing/out-of-order/non-descriptive headings break navigation; Framer's per-layer heading control makes mis-tagging easy: https://www.audioeye.com/post/framer-offers-accessibility-features-but-are-they/

allPatterns.platform: Framer / Webflow link styled by color only (nav, inline text links, variant swatches)
allPatterns.name: Information conveyed by color alone (links, swatches, states)
allPatterns.description: Designers distinguish links from body text, active nav items, or product color/variant swatches using color only — no underline, no text label, no shape/border difference. Color swatches in particular carry the variant name ('Red', 'Forest') purely as a colored circle with no text or accessible name.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup: Read our terms first.
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Tools can't tell that the only cue distinguishing a link from surrounding text is color (they'd have to compare the link's styling to adjacent text and the rest of the page). For color swatches, an unlabeled colored button looks like a generic empty button; recognizing it ENCODES a named option that's conveyed by color alone needs human/visual judgment.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Use-of-color is a top WCAG failure category; design-tool defaults frequently strip link underlines and rely on hue. Background on the swatch/color-only pattern and 1.4.1: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/use-of-color.html and contrast/use-of-color prevalence: https://www.studiolimb.com/guides/wcag-color-contrast-guide.html

allPatterns.platform: Webflow / Bubble CMS-driven 'Learn more' / 'Read more' link lists
allPatterns.name: Repeated generic link text in collection/repeating lists
allPatterns.description: A Collection List or Bubble repeating group renders a card per item, each ending in an identical 'Learn more', 'Read more', or 'View →' link. Out of context the link text is meaningless and screen-reader users hear 'Learn more' a dozen times with no way to tell the destinations apart.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup:
Pricing tiers

Learn more

Case studies

Learn more
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Each link HAS visible text and an href, so it passes the 'link must have a name' check. Judging that 'Learn more' is not descriptive of its purpose — and that an associated heading would have to be programmatically connected to fix it — is a contextual/semantic decision tools can't reliably make (the text is technically present and non-empty).
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Generic 'Learn more / Read more / click here' links are a canonical 2.4.4 failure; CMS card templates mass-produce them. WebAIM and WCAG 2.4.4 guidance: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/link-purpose-in-context.html

allPatterns.platform: Bubble.io input element + 'placeholder as label'
allPatterns.name: Form inputs labeled only by placeholder; aria-label mismatches visible text
allPatterns.description: Bubble inputs commonly ship with a placeholder instead of a programmatic label, or developers paste an aria-label that differs from the visible text. On submit, native required/format errors are not associated with the field (no aria-describedby), so error identification and suggestion are absent for screen-reader users.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup: Invalid
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: If an aria-label is present, axe sees 'input has an accessible name' and passes — it can't know the placeholder disappeared on input or that the aria-label ('Work email') contradicts the visible 'Email address' (a Label-in-Name mismatch). Confirming the error div isn't programmatically tied to the field and isn't announced requires interaction.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Bubble accessibility guidance flags placeholder-as-label and warns that replacing visible labels with aria-label causes a screen-reader/visible-text mismatch; Bubble's own marketplace app audited ~60% accessible: https://www.rapidevelopers.com/bubble-tutorial/designing-accessibility-mind-bubble and https://forum.bubble.io/t/is-bubble-accessible-does-it-comply-with-ada-and-wcag/287361

allPatterns.platform: Webflow / Bubble form success 'toast' or inline confirmation block
allPatterns.name: Submission success/error message not in a live region
allPatterns.description: After form submit, Webflow swaps in its success div (or Bubble shows an alert element) by toggling display, but the message is not a status/live region. Sighted users see 'Thanks, we got it!' or an error banner; screen-reader users get no announcement that submission succeeded or failed.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup:
Thank you! Your submission has been received!
Something went wrong
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: The success/fail divs exist in the DOM at page load with display:none and no role=status / aria-live, which is valid markup. A static scan can't know that toggling display later is a 'status message' that should be announced; verifying the absence of an announcement requires submitting the form with a screen reader running.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Webflow's default form success/fail blocks have no live region; accessible practice is role=status/aria-live for submission feedback (4.1.3). Background: https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/notifications/ and toast/live-region gap discussion: https://a11y-blog.dev/en/articles/aria-live-regions/

allPatterns.platform: Webflow / Framer hover-revealed dropdown menus and tooltips
allPatterns.name: Hover content (mega-menu, tooltip) not dismissible, hoverable, or persistent
allPatterns.description: Mega-menu panels and tooltips built as hover-only Interactions appear on mouseover and vanish the instant the pointer leaves the trigger. There's no Esc-to-dismiss, the revealed panel can't be hovered into without it closing, and it isn't reachable/persistable by keyboard focus.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup:
Products
Item AItem B
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Dismissible/hoverable/persistent (1.4.13) are interaction-time properties. Static analysis sees a nav item with a nested panel and can't determine the panel only appears on :hover, disappears when the pointer moves toward it, and lacks an Esc handler — this requires a human to hover and try to interact with the revealed content.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Classic 1.4.13 failure: content disappears when the mouse moves off the trigger and offers no Esc dismissal; design tools' hover Interactions reproduce exactly this: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/content-on-hover-or-focus.html and https://sarahmhigley.com/writing/tooltips-in-wcag-21/

allPatterns.platform: Notion-published pages (notion.site) and Super.so
allPatterns.name: Generic page <title> and weak heading semantics on exported Notion sites
allPatterns.description: Notion-published pages frequently inherit a generic or duplicated <title> (workspace/page name patterns), and content blocks rely heavily on styled divs; toggles, callouts, and 'columns' don't expose the semantic relationships sighted users perceive. Multiple pages can share an indistinct title, and toggle disclosure widgets often lack proper expanded/collapsed state.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup:
▸ Details
...
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: A <title> exists, so 2.4.2 passes automatically; judging that it's non-descriptive/duplicated across pages needs human comparison. Missing aria-expanded on a toggle MIGHT be linted, but deciding that a styled callout/column block carries structural meaning that isn't conveyed programmatically is a semantic judgment.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Notion accessibility assessments document alt-text, contrast, and tabbing/focus problems and difficulty operating interactive elements with assistive tech: https://ixd.prattsi.org/2024/12/assessing-the-accessibility-of-notion/ and https://www.templates4notion.com/newsletters/better-notion-accessibility

allPatterns.platform: Webflow / Framer template default <title> and page metadata
allPatterns.name: Template-default or placeholder page title shipped to production
allPatterns.description: Cloneable templates and starter projects ship with a placeholder <title> the author never changes — e.g. 'Home', 'Untitled', the template's brand name, or 'Webflow HTML website template'. The page has a title (so it isn't 'empty'), but it doesn't describe the page or site.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup:
<title>Home</title>
<!-- or -->
<title>Untitled — Built in Framer</title>
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: The <title> element is present and non-empty, so automated 2.4.2 checks pass. Recognizing that 'Home', 'Untitled', or a leftover template name fails to identify the page or distinguish it from others requires a human to read it against the page's actual topic and the rest of the site.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Leftover template placeholder titles are a well-known artifact of cloneable Webflow/Framer starters; 2.4.2 requires titles that describe topic or purpose: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/page-titled.html

allPatterns.platform: Framer / Webflow icon-only social and utility buttons (SVG)
allPatterns.name: Icon-only buttons/links with no accessible name
allPatterns.description: Social links, hamburger menu toggles, search and close buttons are placed as inline SVG or icon-font glyphs inside a link/button with no text, no aria-label, and no title — so the accessible name is empty. Common in headers/footers generated from design components.
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: This one IS reliably auto-detectable: axe/Lighthouse flag 'links/buttons must have discernible text' when an interactive element has an empty accessible name. Included for completeness as a common no-code artifact, but a linter catches it.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Webflow's accessibility guidance calls out icon-only buttons missing accessible names as a common critical issue and points to the Designer 'Aria Label' field as the fix: https://webflow.com/accessibility/checklist and audit-tool coverage: https://compliscan.ai/accessibility-checker/webflow

allPatterns.platform: Webflow / Framer hero text baked into an exported image or background
allPatterns.name: Images of text in hero/banner graphics
allPatterns.description: To preserve exact typography, designers export a hero headline, promotional banner, or pricing graphic as a flattened PNG/JPG (or set it as a CSS background-image) instead of live text. The 'text' is pixels: it can't be resized/restyled, and if alt is missing or generic the content is also lost to screen readers.
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Nothing in the markup declares that an image's pixels contain readable text; an automated tool can't OCR/decide an image is 'an image of text' that could have been real text (1.4.5) vs. a legitimate photo/logo. Even an image with alt passes 1.1.1 — judging it's text-as-image needs human visual inspection.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Design-to-site workflows commonly flatten styled headlines to images to preserve fonts; 1.4.5 prohibits images of text except logos/essential cases: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/images-of-text.html

allPatterns.platform: React/Vue/Angular SPA with client-side router (React Router, Vue Router)
allPatterns.name: <title> never updates on client-side route change
allPatterns.description: In an SPA the router swaps the view via the History API without a document reload, but the developer never updates document.title. Every "page" therefore shares the one <title> baked into index.html (e.g. "React App" or the home-page title). Screen-reader users get the same title announced on every navigation, and the browser tab/history/bookmarks are all identically and uselessly named.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup:
<!-- index.html ships once; SPA never rewrites it on navigate -->
<head><title>My React App</title></head>
<!-- user navigates Home -> /pricing -> /contact, title stays "My React App" the whole time -->
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: axe/Lighthouse load one URL and see a present, non-empty <title>, so 2.4.2 passes. The defect is the absence of a CHANGE across route transitions plus the title being semantically wrong/generic for the current view — a temporal + semantic judgment no single-snapshot DOM scan makes.
allPatterns.realWorldNote: Documented as a top SPA a11y mistake; the oaf-react-router library exists specifically to set the page title after navigation, and Kitty Giraudel wrote a dedicated guide on accessible titles in single-page React apps. https://kittygiraudel.com/2020/01/15/accessible-title-in-a-single-page-react-application/

allPatterns.platform: React Router / Vue Router / Angular Router SPA
allPatterns.name: No focus reset or route announcement on navigation
allPatterns.description: After a client-side route change the new view is rendered but keyboard focus stays on the link that was clicked (or is lost to <body>) and nothing is announced via a live region. A screen-reader user hears no indication that navigation occurred; a keyboard user must tab from wherever focus was stranded. There is no route-announcer and focus is not moved to the new page heading.
allPatterns.typicalMarkup:
Pricing

Pricing

...
allPatterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Focus location after a JS navigation and the presence/firing of a route-announcer live region are runtime behaviors triggered by user interaction.
