2.1.1.platform: Shopify / WooCommerce — AJAX filter / faceted search sidebar
2.1.1.name: Facet filtering updates grid silently; no result-count announcement
2.1.1.description: Selecting a filter checkbox (size, color, price) re-renders the product grid via AJAX with no page reload. The new result count ('24 products') and any 'No results' state are not in a live region, so screen reader users don't know the grid changed or how many products remain. Some themes also replace native checkboxes with styled divs that lose keyboard operability.

2.1.1.whyAutoToolsMiss: On the initial static snapshot the markup is valid (labeled checkboxes, a count div). The defect appears only when a filter fires and content swaps without an announcement — a runtime behavior. Whether the count and no-results state qualify as status messages requiring aria-live is an intent-based judgment scanners can't make.
2.1.1.realWorldNote: Equalize Digital's FacetWP audit and Scott O'Hara's 'dynamic results' guidance cover exactly this; accessibility-test.org documents ecommerce faceted-search live-region gaps. https://equalizedigital.com/testing-facetwp-for-accessibility/ ; https://accessibility-test.org/blog/compliance/accessibility-for-e-commerce-product-filtering-and-faceted-search/

2.1.1.platform: Wix Stores / headless React storefronts — icon-only controls
2.1.1.name: div/span 'button' with visual label mismatching its accessible name
2.1.1.description: Cart, wishlist, quick-add and quantity controls are built as <div> or <span> with click handlers and an icon. Either there is no accessible name at all, or an aria-label was copy-pasted/templated so it mismatches the visible glyph or tooltip (e.g. a heart icon labeled 'button', or a '+' quantity stepper whose aria-label says 'Decrease'). The visible text/icon and the programmatic name disagree.
2.1.1.whyAutoToolsMiss: A linter flags the second case (clickable span with no name / no role / no keyboard handler) — that part is auto-detectable. But the first case has a role, tabindex, and an aria-label, so axe passes it; detecting that the label 'Decrease' contradicts the visible '+' glyph requires reading the icon and comparing it to the name — a visual/semantic human judgment (the 'accessible name contains visible label' check needs human eyes on the icon).

2.1.1.platform: Webflow div with Interaction (IX2) used as a button/CTA
2.1.1.name: Clickable div CTA with no role and no accessible name
2.1.1.description: Designers wire a Webflow click Interaction onto a plain Div Block (often containing only an icon or a background image), so the rendered element is a clickable div with no button/link role, not in the tab order, and no accessible name. It looks and behaves like a button visually but is invisible/inoperable to keyboard and screen-reader users.
2.1.1.whyAutoToolsMiss: A bare <div> with a click handler attached via a data-w-id Interaction has no role, no tabindex, and frequently no text — automated scanners do not flag a generic div as a 'control' because nothing in the static DOM declares it interactive; they cannot tell it carries a JS click handler that makes it a de-facto button. Recognizing it as a missing-name control requires a human to see it renders/behaves as a CTA.
2.1.1.realWorldNote: Webflow's own accessibility guidance warns that click triggers should be placed on button elements rather than divs, and that role=button on a div still loses platform behaviors like spacebar activation. See Webflow accessibility checklist / 'The Webflow Way' accessibility docs: https://webflow.com/accessibility/checklist and community guidance at https://www.gracefulwebstudio.com/blog-articles/webflow-video-lightbox-accessibility-and-focus-management

2.1.1.name: Off-screen carousel slides keep focusable controls and links
2.1.1.description: Webflow's Slider hides non-active slides with CSS transforms/opacity (not display:none), so links, buttons, and form fields inside the off-screen slides remain in the tab order. Keyboard users tab into invisible content, focus disappears off-screen, and the slide-dot/arrow controls are often unlabeled icon buttons.

2.1.2.name: Carousel/slider/lightbox not keyboard operable or focus-trapping
2.1.2.description: Wix sliders and popups frequently can't be advanced/controlled by keyboard, and opened lightboxes/popups either don't move focus in, leave focus on the page behind, or trap it without an Esc exit. Arrow controls are mouse-only; the auto-rotating slideshow can't be paused.
2.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: Whether a control is reachable AND operable by keyboard, whether focus moves into a dialog, and whether Esc escapes are runtime/interaction facts. Static scans see divs/images; they can't exercise Tab/Enter/Esc to discover the inoperability or the trap.
2.1.2.realWorldNote: Wix ADA guides: 'Wix sliders are frequently keyboard inaccessible' and 'Wix popups often fail keyboard navigation.' https://www.lowcodewebsite.com/post/wix-accessibility-complete-guide-to-fix-issues-achieve-ada-compliance-2026

2.1.2.platform: Shopify / BigCommerce — quick-view modal (Add to cart from grid)
2.1.2.name: Quick-view modal keyboard trap / no focus return
2.1.2.description: Quick-view modals open over the product grid. Two common failures: (a) focus stays on the underlying page so keyboard users tab through background content behind the overlay, or (b) focus enters the modal but Escape doesn't close it and Tab can cycle but never escape, and on close focus is not returned to the triggering 'Quick view' button — keyboard users are stranded or lose their place.
2.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: role=dialog may be present so structural checks pass. The trap, the missing Escape handler, and the failure to restore focus to the trigger are dynamic, interaction-time behaviors that require actually tabbing through the open modal and closing it — automated DOM snapshots don't exercise focus flow or key handlers.
2.1.2.realWorldNote: TestParty's Shopify checkout/keyboard guides explicitly call out 'quick-view modals that trap focus so keyboard users cannot escape' and modals that 'capture focus and never give it back'. https://testparty.ai/blog/shopify-checkout-keyboard-navigation-fixes ; https://testparty.ai/blog/modal-dialog-accessibility

2.4.2.name: System page reuses generic title and has no H1
2.4.2.description: The default 404 page (and some system pages) ships with no option for an H1 and inherits a non-unique page title, so AT users who land there get a page with no main heading and a <title> that doesn't say it's a 'Page Not Found' page, leaving them disoriented about where they are.
2.4.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: A <title> is present and non-empty, so 'document-title' passes; whether it actually describes THIS page (vs. being the generic site title repeated) is a semantic comparison a human must make. A missing h1 is at most a warning, not a hard failure, in most scanners.
2.4.2.realWorldNote: Amy Carney's Squarespace audit: 404 page has 'no H1 heading option available' and is 'missing a unique page title.' https://theamycarney.com/2024/04/02/observations-on-squarespace-accessibility/

2.4.2.platform: WordPress theme demo import / starter templates (Astra, OceanWP, Elementor Kits, Divi Layouts)
2.4.2.name: Placeholder demo content left in production — default title, lorem ipsum, stock alt
2.4.2.description: One-click demo imports populate the site with template defaults that editors forget to replace: the page <title> stays 'My WordPress Site' / 'Just another WordPress site' tagline, headings and links read 'Lorem ipsum dolor', CTA buttons say 'Button Text', and stock images carry the kit's generic alt. Titles don't uniquely describe the page; link text is meaningless Latin.
2.4.2.typicalMarkup:
Lorem Ipsum Dolor

Click Here
2.4.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: A <title> of 'Just another WordPress site' is present and non-empty (2.4.2 passes a presence check); lorem-ipsum link text is non-empty. Recognizing the content is unreplaced placeholder that fails to describe topic/purpose is a semantic judgment a linter can't make.
2.4.2.realWorldNote: Demo/starter imports use lorem ipsum and template defaults; WPBeginner documents importing dummy content; 'Just another WordPress site' is the stock tagline. https://www.wpbeginner.com/wp-themes/how-to-add-dummy-content-for-theme-development-in-wordpress/

2.4.2.name: <title> and H1 never update on client-side route change
2.4.2.description: Navigating from collection to product to cart happens client-side; the document <title> stays at the homepage/store name on every route, and focus is not moved to the new page's H1. Screen reader users hear the same title on every 'page' and get no signal that navigation occurred.
2.4.2.typicalMarkup:
<head><title>Acme Store</title></head>
<!-- after client-side nav to /products/blue-shirt the title is still "Acme Store";
     no React Helmet update, no focus moved to the product <h1> -->
2.4.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: A single-page audit finds a non-empty <title> and passes 2.4.2. The failure is that the title doesn't CHANGE across virtual route transitions and is identical/non-descriptive for each view — a multi-state behavior. Tools scan one DOM state and have no concept of route changes, so they never compare titles across navigations.
2.4.2.realWorldNote: Widely documented SPA failure (Hidde Blog, Kitty Giraudel, Helsinki a11y model): SPAs keep a static <title> unless JS updates it on every route change. https://hidde.blog/accessible-page-titles-in-a-single-page-app/ ; https://saavutettavuusmalli.hel.fi/en/saavutettavuus-palvelukehityksessa/toteutus-ja-ohjelmistotestaus/single-page-applications-spas-notes-on-accessibility/

2.4.2.platform: Framer (and other React SPA exporters: Typedream, Readymag)
2.4.2.name: SPA route change leaves <title> stale and focus unmoved
2.4.2.description: Page-to-page navigation is client-side. The document <title> is not updated on route change, focus stays on the clicked link (or resets to <body>), and there is no route-change announcement. Screen-reader users get no signal a new page loaded and the title still reads the landing page.
2.4.2.typicalMarkup: Pricing

2.4.2.name: Generic page <title> and weak heading semantics on exported Notion sites
2.4.2.description: Notion-published pages frequently inherit a generic or duplicated <title> (workspace/page name patterns), and content blocks rely heavily on styled divs; toggles, callouts, and 'columns' don't expose the semantic relationships sighted users perceive. ▸ Details
...

2.4.2.platform: Webflow / Framer template default <title> and page metadata
2.4.2.name: Template-default or placeholder page title shipped to production
2.4.2.description: Cloneable templates and starter projects ship with a placeholder <title> the author never changes — e.g. 'Home', 'Untitled', the template's brand name, or 'Webflow HTML website template'. The page has a title (so it isn't 'empty'), but it doesn't describe the page or site.
2.4.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: The <title> element is present and non-empty, so automated 2.4.2 checks pass. Recognizing that 'Home', 'Untitled', or a leftover template name fails to identify the page or distinguish it from others requires a human to read it against the page's actual topic and the rest of the site.
2.4.2.realWorldNote: Leftover template placeholder titles are a well-known artifact of cloneable Webflow/Framer starters; 2.4.2 requires titles that describe topic or purpose: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/page-titled.html

2.4.2.platform: React/Vue/Angular SPA with client-side router (React Router, Vue Router)
2.4.2.name: <title> never updates on client-side route change
2.4.2.description: In an SPA the router swaps the view via the History API without a document reload, but the developer never updates document.title. Every "page" therefore shares the one <title> baked into index.html (e.g. "React App" or the home-page title). Screen-reader users get the same title announced on every navigation, and the browser tab/history/bookmarks are all identically and uselessly named.
2.4.2.typicalMarkup:
<!-- index.html ships once; SPA never rewrites it on navigate -->
<head><title>My React App</title></head>
<!-- user navigates Home -> /pricing -> /contact, title stays "My React App" the whole time -->
2.4.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: axe/Lighthouse load one URL and see a present, non-empty <title>, so 2.4.2 passes. The defect is the absence of a CHANGE across route transitions plus the title being semantically wrong/generic for the current view — a temporal + semantic judgment no single-snapshot DOM scan makes.
2.4.2.realWorldNote: Documented as a top SPA a11y mistake; the oaf-react-router library exists specifically to set the page title after navigation, and Kitty Giraudel wrote a dedicated guide on accessible titles in single-page React apps. https://kittygiraudel.com/2020/01/15/accessible-title-in-a-single-page-react-application/

2.4.3.name: DOM/reading order diverges from visual order on overlapping layouts
2.4.3.description: Wix's drag-anywhere canvas positions elements absolutely; the algorithm that derives DOM order from on-screen coordinates can mis-order overlapping, stacked, or strip-based sections, so keyboard Tab order and screen-reader reading order jump around (e.g., footer CTA before main content, a caption before its image, a price before the product name).
2.4.3.typicalMarkup:
Add to cart
Handmade Mug — $24
2.4.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: Automated tools generally cannot determine the 'correct' meaningful sequence — they don't know the visually-intended reading order, so they can't tell that DOM order contradicts it. Detecting the mismatch requires a human comparing the visual layout to the tab/reading order.
2.4.3.realWorldNote: Wix Engineering describes building an algorithm to make DOM order reflect visual position precisely because the canvas otherwise breaks navigation order; Wix support has a dedicated 'Checking and Adjusting a Site's DOM Order' article. https://www.wix.engineering/post/the-story-of-making-wix-accessible

2.4.3.name: Silent add-to-cart: drawer/toast update not in a live region
2.4.3.description: Clicking 'Add to cart' updates a cart-count bubble and slides open a cart drawer or shows a toast, but the success message is injected into a normal <div> with no role=status / aria-live. 2.4.3.name: Off-screen carousel slides keep focusable controls and links
2.4.3.description: Webflow's Slider hides non-active slides with CSS transforms/opacity (not display:none), so links, buttons, and form fields inside the off-screen slides remain in the tab order. Keyboard users tab into invisible content, focus disappears off-screen, and the slide-dot/arrow controls are often unlabeled icon buttons.
2.4.3.typicalMarkup: Shop now
2.4.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: The off-screen slide is still visible to the accessibility tree (no display:none / aria-hidden), so scanners see normal in-DOM links and report nothing wrong; detecting that focus visually 'leaves the screen' onto a translated-off slide requires running the keyboard sequence and watching where the focus ring goes — a dynamic, visual check tools don't perform.
2.4.3.realWorldNote: Accessibility guidance for sliders specifies off-screen slides must be hidden via display:none/visibility:hidden or aria-hidden + tabindex=-1, which Webflow's default Slider does not do: https://dev.to/jasonwebb/how-to-build-a-more-accessible-carousel-or-slider-35lp and https://www.flowradar.com/answer/fix-issue-slider-webflow-not-accessible-screen-readers

2.4.3.name: Lightbox opens without focus trap, dialog role, or labeled close
2.4.3.description: Webflow's built-in Lightbox opens an overlay but does not trap focus (Tab leaves the modal to the page behind it), has no role=dialog / aria-modal, no accessible name on the dialog, and the close 'X' is an unlabeled icon. Esc behavior and focus return to the trigger are not handled.
2.4.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: A missing focus trap is a behavioral property: nothing in the static markup is 'invalid', so axe/Lighthouse cannot detect that Tab escapes the open overlay. The unlabeled close MIGHT be flagged, but confirming the dialog lacks a name and that focus returns to the trigger requires opening it and operating it by keyboard.
2.4.3.realWorldNote: Documented that the Webflow lightbox lacks a focus trap (users can tab out), is missing a descriptive accessible name on the dialog, and needs custom code/ARIA to fix: https://www.gracefulwebstudio.com/blog-articles/webflow-video-lightbox-accessibility-and-focus-management and Webflow's own checklist task 'Ensure modals are keyboard navigable': https://webflow.com/accessibility/checklist/task/ensure-modals-are-keyboard-navigable

2.4.3.platform: Webflow / Framer absolute-positioned layout (CSS grid-area, position:absolute, flex order)
2.4.3.name: Visual order diverges from DOM/tab order in free-canvas layouts
2.4.3.description: On a free design canvas, authors drag elements into a visual arrangement while the DOM source order stays whatever was authored. Absolute positioning, CSS order, and grid placement make the reading/tab order jump around — e.g., a CTA visually at top-left is last in the DOM, or a sidebar reads before the main column for a screen reader.
2.4.3.typicalMarkup:
Primary CTA
Legal footnote
Headline
2.4.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: Both the DOM order and the CSS are individually valid; determining that the resulting tab/reading order is 'illogical' relative to the visual layout requires a human to compare what they SEE to the order focus actually moves — automated tools have no model of the intended visual narrative.
2.4.3.realWorldNote: Webflow's checklist 'Ensure focus order is logical' explicitly warns that arranging elements with CSS instead of the Navigator yields nonlinear/illogical focus order; WCAG technique C27 covers DOM-vs-visual order: https://webflow.com/accessibility/checklist/task/ensure-focus-order-is-logical and https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG20-TECHS/C27.html

2.4.3.name: Background page not inert / aria-hidden focus conflict behind modal
2.4.3.description: When a Bootstrap/custom modal opens, the underlying page is not made inert and is not hidden from AT (or, conversely, aria-hidden="true" is placed on an ancestor that still contains the focused trigger). Screen-reader users can read and tab into the page behind the dialog, and focus can land on aria-hidden content, producing the "focusable element inside aria-hidden" conflict.

2.4.4.name: Triple-redundant 'Read More →' links sharing one destination
2.4.4.description: Each summary item auto-emits the thumbnail image, the post title, AND a 'Read More →' link, all three pointing to the same post URL. Screen-reader users tabbing the link list hear 'Read More, link / Read More, link / Read More, link' with no way to distinguish posts, and the same destination is reachable three times. The 'Read More →' text cannot be edited or removed through built-in settings.
2.4.4.typicalMarkup: Spring Tips Read More →
2.4.4.whyAutoToolsMiss: Each <a> has non-empty text ('Read More →'), so link-name checks pass; the redundancy/ambiguity is only a problem when the links are read out of context as a list, which requires human judgment about whether the link purpose is determinable. Tools can't know the three links go to the same place is intended vs. confusing.
2.4.4.realWorldNote: Amy Carney's hands-on Squarespace audit: 'Redundant links: image, heading, and Read More all link to same destination' and the Read More link cannot be customized or unlinked. https://theamycarney.com/2024/04/02/observations-on-squarespace-accessibility/

2.4.4.platform: Elementor Icon Box / Icon List widget (Font Awesome icon fonts)
2.4.4.name: Icon-only link/button whose accessible name is the icon glyph or empty
2.4.4.description: Icon Box and social-icon widgets render a link wrapping only a Font Awesome <i> with no text. The accessible name comes out empty (empty link) or, when the icon font exposes a glyph/private-use character, a screen reader announces a meaningless symbol name. CSS pseudo-element icons (::before content) can be read aloud as random characters bearing no relation to the visible icon.
2.4.4.whyAutoToolsMiss: When the accessible name is truly empty, axe catches it (link has no discernible text). But when the icon font leaks a glyph name or a pseudo-element character into the name, the link is technically 'named' and tools pass it while the announced name ('private-use-F07A') is meaningless — judging that requires hearing what's announced vs. seeing the cart icon.
2.4.4.realWorldNote: Elementor docs and abrightclearweb note Icon widgets 'create empty links and adjacent identical links'; Divi review notes CSS pseudo-element icons cause screen readers to 'announce the symbol's name, which has no semantic relationship.' https://www.abrightclearweb.com/elementor-accessibility/ and https://elevagedigital.com/improving-wordpress-divi-accessibility/

2.4.4.platform: Elementor Image Carousel / Slides widget, Divi Slider, Smart Slider 3
2.4.4.name: Auto-advancing carousel: icon-only controls + slide content/links hidden from AT
2.4.4.description: Slider widgets auto-rotate with no clearly labeled pause/stop control. Prev/next arrows are icon-only with empty accessible names; pagination dots are unlabeled buttons. Off-screen slides are not consistently hidden from the accessibility tree, so screen-reader users encounter duplicate/moving content and links to slides they can't see.
2.4.4.whyAutoToolsMiss: Empty arrow/dot names are partially catchable, but judging that hidden slides leak focusable links into the tab order, and that there is no labeled pause control, requires observing the running carousel and its focus behavior across slide states.
2.4.4.realWorldNote: Elementor audit: 'Images in the carousel advance automatically every three seconds with no mechanism for pausing, stopping, or hiding.' https://www.accessibilitychecker.org/blog/elementor-website-accessibility/

Out of context the buttons are indistinguishable by name, so a screen-reader user navigating buttons can't tell the Basic from the Pro plan. It looks and behaves like a button visually but is invisible/inoperable to keyboard and screen-reader users.

Recognizing it as a missing-name control requires a human to see it renders/behaves as a CTA.

Keyboard users tab into invisible content, focus disappears off-screen, and the slide-dot/arrow controls are often unlabeled icon buttons.

2.4.7.name: focus:outline-none with no replacement focus ring
2.4.7.description: Developers apply Tailwind's focus:outline-none (often to kill the default blue ring on inputs/buttons) but never add a focus-visible:ring/outline replacement. 2.4.10.platform: Gutenberg blocks / page-builder sections used as visual styling (Heading block, Divi Text module set to H-tag)

Editors pick heading tags by how big they look. A section header is set to H4 because H2 'looks too big', producing H1 then H4 with no H2/H3. Conversely, bold styled text that visually functions as a heading is left as a

Welcome

Our Services

Pricing

Tools can flag a skipped level (H1->H4) but cannot decide that styled bold

SHOULD be a heading, nor whether a heading is descriptive of the section it labels. That mapping of visual prominence and meaning to correct level/semantics is human judgment.

2.4.10.typicalMarkup:
Acme

Build faster

Features

Pricing

3.3.1.name: Success/confirmation message injected without a live region
3.3.1.description: On submit, the form swaps in a visible 'Thank you, your message has been sent' confirmation in place of the form, but the inserted node is not a role=status / aria-live region and focus is not moved to it. Sighted users see success; screen-reader users hear nothing and may believe the submission failed and re-submit.

3.3.1.whyAutoToolsMiss: The message is valid visible text in the DOM; a static scan sees correct markup and no error. Catching it requires dynamically submitting the form AND observing (with AT or by checking for a live region / focus move) that the status change is never announced — a behavioral, human-in-the-loop check.
3.3.1.realWorldNote: Amy Carney's Squarespace audit: 'Same-page confirmation messages don't alert screen reader users of state changes' and 'error lists aren't linked to inputs or focused.' https://theamycarney.com/2024/04/02/observations-on-squarespace-accessibility/

3.3.1.platform: Squarespace / Wix contact & booking forms (custom-styled fields)
3.3.1.name: Placeholder used as the only label; errors not programmatically tied to fields

3.3.1.platform: Elementor Form widget / Divi Contact Form / WPForms — submission feedback
3.3.1.name: Success/error toast not in a live region; errors flagged by color only
3.3.1.description: After AJAX form submit, the success or error message is injected into a <div> that is not a live region and not focused, so screen readers never announce it. 3.3.1.name: Field errors shown as red text only, not associated with the input

3.3.1.name: Form inputs labeled only by placeholder; aria-label mismatches visible text

3.3.1.name: Validation error not programmatically associated with the field

3.3.1.platform: React conditionally-rendered form error summary / aria-live status
3.3.1.name: Submit-time errors rendered but not announced; focus not moved
3.3.1.description: On form submit, a React app conditionally renders an error summary or per-field messages into the DOM, but the container is not a live region and focus is not moved to it. 4.1.2.platform: Divi / Elementor button modules with icons and 'global' default labels (Pricing Table, CTA)
4.1.2.name: Multiple buttons with identical generic accessible name ('Get Started', 'Submit')
4.1.2.description: Pricing-table and CTA modules ship every plan's button reading the same default ('Get Started' / 'Buy Now' / 'Learn More'). Out of context the buttons are indistinguishable by name, so a screen-reader user navigating buttons can't tell the Basic from the Pro plan. Editors leave the default because per-button custom labels 'look kludgy.'
4.1.2.typicalMarkup:
Basic

...Get Started

Pro

...Get Started

Enterprise

...Get Started
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: Each button has a valid, non-empty name, so 4.1.2 passes and there's no duplicate-id type error. Recognizing the three 'Get Started' names are ambiguous and need to encode the plan requires understanding the page's meaning and the navigate-by-button workflow.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: Beaver Builder review: Pricing Table 'buttons all say the same thing – Get Started, and while you could edit this... it would make the buttons look kludgy.' https://wpshout.com/beaver-builder-accessibility/

4.1.2.platform: WooCommerce / Elementor product loop on Storefront, Astra, Divi shops
4.1.2.name: Color/variant swatches conveyed by color only; 'Add to cart' names not unique
4.1.2.description: Product variation swatches are colored squares/links with no text or accessible name ('Red', 'Blue' is visual-only), so the choice is unperceivable without color. In the shop grid every product's 'Add to cart' / 'Select options' button has the same name, indistinguishable by product when navigating by button.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup: Add to cart
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: Color-only meaning (1.4.1) is not statically detectable — a tool can't know the red square MEANS 'red' with no text backup. Repeated 'Add to cart' names are valid names. Both require understanding what the visual conveys and the by-button navigation experience.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: WooCommerce color-swatch plugins render color-only links; equalizedigital and WebAIM repeatedly flag color-only controls and duplicate 'add to cart' button names as a top WordPress-shop barrier. https://equalizedigital.com/accessibility-checker/

4.1.2.platform: Elementor Tabs widget / Beaver Builder Tabs / Divi Tabs module
4.1.2.name: Tab panel content not associated/announced; div tabs missing roles
4.1.2.description: Builder 'tabs' render as styled divs. Either the tablist/tab/tabpanel roles and aria-controls/aria-selected are absent (so it's just clickable divs), or the roles exist but the panel content isn't reliably exposed when a tab is activated. Selecting a tab by keyboard may not move focus or announce the newly revealed panel.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup:
• Description
  • Reviews
...
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: Plain divs with click handlers raise no role/value error in a scanner (nothing claims to be a tab). Where roles do exist, confirming the active panel's content is actually announced on switch needs screen-reader testing, not static analysis.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: Beaver Builder review: with tabs 'the content of an expanded tab isn't reliably read out.' https://wpshout.com/beaver-builder-accessibility/

4.1.2.platform: Elementor / Divi 'div as button' CTA blocks, animated counters, hotspot widgets
4.1.2.name: Div with onClick acting as a button — wrong/absent role, no keyboard, name mismatch
4.1.2.description: A styled <div> (or <a href="#">) carries a JS click handler and visually reads as a button. It exposes no button role, isn't in the tab order, and Enter/Space don't activate it. Where an aria-label is added it can mismatch the visible label (e.g. visible 'Start your free trial', aria-label left as a generic 'button' from a template), so the accessible name doesn't contain the visible text.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup: Start your free trial
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: A div with onClick and no role is invisible to the accessibility tree, so some scanners simply don't see a control to test. Detecting the visible-vs-accessible name mismatch and that it should be a keyboard-operable button requires comparing what's seen to what's announced.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: Elementor #25128: aria-label custom attribute doesn't reach the <a>, producing name mismatches; div-button anti-pattern is endemic to builder CTA modules. https://github.com/elementor/elementor/issues/25128

4.1.2.platform: Shopify Dawn theme — product variant picker (color)
4.1.2.name: Color-only variant swatches with no text alternative
4.1.2.description: Color variant options render as colored circles/squares (radio inputs visually replaced by background-color chips). The only way to know which color is which is to see the chip; the accessible name is often the hex/handle or absent, so a screen reader announces 'option 1, option 2' or just the color value, and there is no non-color cue distinguishing selected vs available swatches. Color is the sole means of conveying the choice.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup: Color
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: The radio inputs are technically labeled (the <label for> exists and the value attribute carries the color name), so axe/Lighthouse see a valid, named form control and pass it. They cannot perceive that the swatch communicates the choice purely through a CSS background-color, nor judge whether the visible chip and the accessible name actually correspond, nor whether selection state has a non-color indicator.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: Shopify Dawn ships swatches as color chips and merchants add color-only swatches via tutorials (made4uo.com swatch guide; Dawn issue #3112 on color swatches). Audits of Dawn flag color contrast and ARIA on swatches. https://github.com/Shopify/dawn/issues/3112 ; https://testparty.ai/blog/shopify-dawn-theme-accessibility

4.1.2.platform: Magento Luma / third-party review widgets — star ratings
4.1.2.name: Star rating rendered with CSS width %, no text alternative
4.1.2.description: Average rating shows as filled/empty stars implemented as a background-image bar with inline width (e.g. width:80%). There is no aria-label or visually-hidden text, so screen readers announce nothing, or announce a raw '80%' with no unit, instead of 'Rated 4 out of 5 stars'. Same in third-party Shopify review apps.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup: Rating:
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: There is no to require alt on — the stars are CSS background images, which automated scanners ignore entirely. A title='80%' may exist but tools won't judge that '80%' is meaningless as a rating. Determining that this visual is conveying a 4-of-5 rating that needs a textual equivalent is a human contextual/visual judgment.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: Magento Luma uses CSS-width rating bars; TestParty's Shopify barriers list cites third-party 'review widgets with star ratings without text alternatives'. https://testparty.ai/blog/beyond-alt-text-hidden-shopify-accessibility-barriers

4.1.2.platform: Wix Stores / headless React storefronts — icon-only controls
4.1.2.name: div/span 'button' with visual label mismatching its accessible name
4.1.2.description: Cart, wishlist, quick-add and quantity controls are built as <div> or <span> with click handlers and an icon. Either there is no accessible name at all, or an aria-label was copy-pasted/templated so it mismatches the visible glyph or tooltip (e.g. a heart icon labeled 'button', or a '+' quantity stepper whose aria-label says 'Decrease'). The visible text/icon and the programmatic name disagree.
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: A linter flags the second case (clickable span with no name / no role / no keyboard handler) — that part is auto-detectable. But the first case has a role, tabindex, and an aria-label, so axe passes it; detecting that the label 'Decrease' contradicts the visible '+' glyph requires reading the icon and comparing it to the name — a visual/semantic human judgment (the 'accessible name contains visible label' check needs human eyes on the icon).
4.1.2.realWorldNote: Wix guidance notes 'missing or inappropriately applied ARIA labels' as a critical screen-reader issue and that some elements need manual fixing; TestParty lists wishlist/quick-add 'icon-only buttons without labels'. https://accessibe.com/blog/knowledgebase/wix-website-accessibility ; https://testparty.ai/blog/beyond-alt-text-hidden-shopify-accessibility-barriers

4.1.2.platform: WooCommerce / Magento — checkout form validation
4.1.2.name: Field errors shown as red text only, not associated with the input
4.1.2.description: On checkout submit, invalid fields turn red and a message like 'This field is required' appears, but the message is a sibling div not linked via aria-describedby/aria-errormessage, the input has no aria-invalid, and color is the only cue marking which fields failed. Screen reader users tabbing the form don't hear which fields are in error or why.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup: This field is required.
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: The error text exists and the label is associated, so structural scanners pass. They cannot verify at runtime that submitting produced an error that is (a) tied to the right field programmatically and (b) not communicated by red color alone. Confirming the association and that the message is meaningful requires submitting the form and inspecting the error/field relationship — a human/runtime judgment.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: Generic but rampant in ecommerce checkout; DigitalA11y and AccessiCart describe exactly this 3.3.1 pattern (red-only, unassociated errors) and call it out for checkout flows. https://accessicart.com/wcag-level-a-sc-3-3-1-error-identification/ ; https://www.digitala11y.com/understanding-sc-3-3-1-error-identification/

4.1.2.platform: Generic ecommerce — required-field marking on cart/checkout/newsletter forms
4.1.2.name: Required fields indicated by red asterisk/color only
4.1.2.description: Checkout, account, and newsletter signup forms mark required inputs with a red asterisk styled purely via color (no 'required' word, no required/aria-required attribute, asterisk not in the label text). Users who don't perceive the color, or screen reader users, don't learn the field is mandatory until submission fails.
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: The label is associated and present, so the form passes label checks. Whether 'required' is conveyed by more than color, whether the asterisk's meaning is explained, and whether aria-required is set are partly structural but partly contextual — tools don't flag a red asterisk as a use-of-color failure because they can't tie the color to the 'required' meaning. Recognizing the instruction is missing needs human review.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: TestParty 'Beyond Alt Text' lists 'red asterisks only marking required fields without text labels' as a Shopify use-of-color (1.4.1) barrier. https://testparty.ai/blog/beyond-alt-text-hidden-shopify-accessibility-barriers

4.1.2.platform: Webflow div with Interaction (IX2) used as a button/CTA
4.1.2.name: Clickable div CTA with no role and no accessible name
4.1.2.description: Designers wire a Webflow click Interaction onto a plain Div Block (often containing only an icon or a background image), so the rendered element is a clickable div with no button/link role, not in the tab order, and no accessible name. It looks and behaves like a button visually but is invisible/inoperable to keyboard and screen-reader users.
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: A bare <div> with a click handler attached via a data-w-id Interaction has no role, no tabindex, and frequently no text — automated scanners do not flag a generic div as a 'control' because nothing in the static DOM declares it interactive; they cannot tell it carries a JS click handler that makes it a de-facto button. Recognizing it as a missing-name control requires a human to see it renders/behaves as a CTA.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: Webflow's own accessibility guidance warns that click triggers should be placed on button elements rather than divs, and that role=button on a div still loses platform behaviors like spacebar activation. See Webflow accessibility checklist / 'The Webflow Way' accessibility docs: https://webflow.com/accessibility/checklist and community guidance at https://www.gracefulwebstudio.com/blog-articles/webflow-video-lightbox-accessibility-and-focus-management

4.1.2.platform: Webflow native Slider component
4.1.2.name: Off-screen carousel slides keep focusable controls and links
4.1.2.description: Webflow's Slider hides non-active slides with CSS transforms/opacity (not display:none), so links, buttons, and form fields inside the off-screen slides remain in the tab order. Keyboard users tab into invisible content, focus disappears off-screen, and the slide-dot/arrow controls are often unlabeled icon buttons.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup: Shop now
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: The off-screen slide is still visible to the accessibility tree (no display:none / aria-hidden), so scanners see normal in-DOM links and report nothing wrong; detecting that focus visually 'leaves the screen' onto a translated-off slide requires running the keyboard sequence and watching where the focus ring goes — a dynamic, visual check tools don't perform.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: Accessibility guidance for sliders specifies off-screen slides must be hidden via display:none/visibility:hidden or aria-hidden + tabindex=-1, which Webflow's default Slider does not do: https://dev.to/jasonwebb/how-to-build-a-more-accessible-carousel-or-slider-35lp and https://www.flowradar.com/answer/fix-issue-slider-webflow-not-accessible-screen-readers

4.1.2.platform: Webflow native Lightbox component
4.1.2.name: Lightbox opens without focus trap, dialog role, or labeled close
4.1.2.description: Webflow's built-in Lightbox opens an overlay but does not trap focus (Tab leaves the modal to the page behind it), has no role=dialog / aria-modal, no accessible name on the dialog, and the close 'X' is an unlabeled icon. Esc behavior and focus return to the trigger are not handled.
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: A missing focus trap is a behavioral property: nothing in the static markup is 'invalid', so axe/Lighthouse cannot detect that Tab escapes the open overlay. The unlabeled close MIGHT be flagged, but confirming the dialog lacks a name and that focus returns to the trigger requires opening it and operating it by keyboard.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: Documented that the Webflow lightbox lacks a focus trap (users can tab out), is missing a descriptive accessible name on the dialog, and needs custom code/ARIA to fix: https://www.gracefulwebstudio.com/blog-articles/webflow-video-lightbox-accessibility-and-focus-management and Webflow's own checklist task 'Ensure modals are keyboard navigable': https://webflow.com/accessibility/checklist/task/ensure-modals-are-keyboard-navigable

4.1.2.platform: Framer / Webflow link styled by color only (nav, inline text links, variant swatches)
4.1.2.name: Information conveyed by color alone (links, swatches, states)
4.1.2.description: Designers distinguish links from body text, active nav items, or product color/variant swatches using color only — no underline, no text label, no shape/border difference. Color swatches in particular carry the variant name ('Red', 'Forest') purely as a colored circle with no text or accessible name.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup: Read our terms first.
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: Tools can't tell that the only cue distinguishing a link from surrounding text is color (they'd have to compare the link's styling to adjacent text and the rest of the page). For color swatches, an unlabeled colored button looks like a generic empty button; recognizing it ENCODES a named option that's conveyed by color alone needs human/visual judgment.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: Use-of-color is a top WCAG failure category; design-tool defaults frequently strip link underlines and rely on hue. Background on the swatch/color-only pattern and 1.4.1: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/use-of-color.html and contrast/use-of-color prevalence: https://www.studiolimb.com/guides/wcag-color-contrast-guide.html

4.1.2.platform: Bubble.io input element + 'placeholder as label'
4.1.2.name: Form inputs labeled only by placeholder; aria-label mismatches visible text
4.1.2.description: Bubble inputs commonly ship with a placeholder instead of a programmatic label, or developers paste an aria-label that differs from the visible text. On submit, native required/format errors are not associated with the field (no aria-describedby), so error identification and suggestion are absent for screen-reader users.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup: Invalid
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: If an aria-label is present, axe sees 'input has an accessible name' and passes — it can't know the placeholder disappeared on input or that the aria-label ('Work email') contradicts the visible 'Email address' (a Label-in-Name mismatch). Confirming the error div isn't programmatically tied to the field and isn't announced requires interaction.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: Bubble accessibility guidance flags placeholder-as-label and warns that replacing visible labels with aria-label causes a screen-reader/visible-text mismatch; Bubble's own marketplace app audited ~60% accessible: https://www.rapidevelopers.com/bubble-tutorial/designing-accessibility-mind-bubble and https://forum.bubble.io/t/is-bubble-accessible-does-it-comply-with-ada-and-wcag/287361

4.1.2.platform: Notion-published pages (notion.site) and Super.so
4.1.2.name: Generic page <title> and weak heading semantics on exported Notion sites
4.1.2.description: Notion-published pages frequently inherit a generic or duplicated <title> (workspace/page name patterns), and content blocks rely heavily on styled divs; toggles, callouts, and 'columns' don't expose the semantic relationships sighted users perceive. Multiple pages can share an indistinct title, and toggle disclosure widgets often lack proper expanded/collapsed state.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup:
▸ Details
...
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: A <title> exists, so 2.4.2 passes automatically; judging that it's non-descriptive/duplicated across pages needs human comparison. Missing aria-expanded on a toggle MIGHT be linted, but deciding that a styled callout/column block carries structural meaning that isn't conveyed programmatically is a semantic judgment.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: Notion accessibility assessments document alt-text, contrast, and tabbing/focus problems and difficulty operating interactive elements with assistive tech: https://ixd.prattsi.org/2024/12/assessing-the-accessibility-of-notion/ and https://www.templates4notion.com/newsletters/better-notion-accessibility

4.1.2.platform: Framer / Webflow icon-only social and utility buttons (SVG)
4.1.2.name: Icon-only buttons/links with no accessible name
4.1.2.description: Social links, hamburger menu toggles, search and close buttons are placed as inline SVG or icon-font glyphs inside a link/button with no text, no aria-label, and no title — so the accessible name is empty. Common in headers/footers generated from design components.
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: This one IS reliably auto-detectable: axe/Lighthouse flag 'links/buttons must have discernible text' when an interactive element has an empty accessible name. Included for completeness as a common no-code artifact, but a linter catches it.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: Webflow's accessibility guidance calls out icon-only buttons missing accessible names as a common critical issue and points to the Designer 'Aria Label' field as the fix: https://webflow.com/accessibility/checklist and audit-tool coverage: https://compliscan.ai/accessibility-checker/webflow

4.1.2.platform: Font Awesome (web-font / CSS pseudo-element icons)
4.1.2.name: Decorative icon-font glyph read aloud (or interactive icon with no name)
4.1.2.description: Font Awesome's web-font method renders a glyph via a CSS ::before pseudo-element on an empty <i>/<span>. If the author omits aria-hidden="true", some AT/browsers expose the private-use Unicode glyph as garbage or a literal character name. Conversely, when the icon IS the only content of a link/button and is hidden (or carries no text alternative), the control has no accessible name at all.
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: Whether the glyph is decorative (needs aria-hidden) or meaningful (needs a label) is a semantic call. An empty <i> with classes has no text for a linter to evaluate, and the icon-only-link-with-no-name case is sometimes caught by axe but not when a stray whitespace/title gives a spurious name; deciding the name is wrong/missing in context needs human review.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: Font Awesome's own accessibility docs state web-font icons must be manually given aria-hidden if decorative and role=img + visually-hidden text if meaningful. https://docs.fontawesome.com/web/dig-deeper/accessibility

4.1.2.platform: Inline SVG icon system (Heroicons, Lucide, Feather, Material Symbols inlined)
4.1.2.name: Icon-only button/link with no accessible name (SVG provides none)
4.1.2.description: A button or link whose only content is an inline <svg> with no <title>, no aria-label on the control, and no visually-hidden text. Screen readers announce just "button" / "link". Even when a <title> is added inside the SVG, several browser+SR combinations fail to surface it as the control's name, so it must be on the button.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup:
<button class="icon-btn">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M..."/></svg>
</button>
<!-- announced as just "button" -->
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: axe and Lighthouse DO reliably flag a button/link with an empty accessible name ("Buttons must have discernible text"), so a linter catches the no-name case. (Choosing a CORRECT label, however, would need human judgment — but the bare detection is automatable, hence flagged false.)
4.1.2.realWorldNote: Sara Soueidan and CSS-Tricks document that there is no reliable way to use an SVG as the sole accessible name and that icon-only controls need aria-label on the control. https://www.sarasoueidan.com/blog/accessible-icon-buttons/

4.1.2.platform: Custom div/span "button" (React component with role="button")
4.1.2.name: Label-in-name mismatch: aria-label differs from visible text
4.1.2.description: A component renders a clickable element showing one visible label but sets an aria-label/aria-labelledby that says something different (e.g. visible "Submit", aria-label "Submit form"; or visible "Buy" with aria-label "Add to cart"). Speech-input users who say the visible word cannot activate it, and the announced name conflicts with what is seen.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup: Submit
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: axe's label-content-name-mismatch rule catches some cases, but it only fires when the visible text is NOT contained in the accessible name; many real mismatches (paraphrases, icon+text where the visible text is partly present, or labelledby pointing at a different node) slip through, and judging whether the names are semantically equivalent for a user requires reading both as a human.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: Deque axe rule label-content-name-mismatch and W3C ARIA14 / SC 2.5.3 Label in Name describe this; Ben Myers warns against aria-label on elements with visible text. https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.7/label-content-name-mismatch

4.1.2.platform: E-commerce product page (React/Vue store, Shopify/SFCC swatch components)
4.1.2.name: Color-only variant swatches with no text label or non-color selected state
4.1.2.description: Product color/variant options render as colored squares (often div with a background-color and a click handler) with no accompanying text name, and the selected swatch is indicated only by a colored ring. Users who cannot perceive color cannot tell which variant they are choosing or which is currently selected; the swatches may also lack accessible names entirely.
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: Whether information (the color name / which is selected) is conveyed by color ALONE requires understanding what the UI means and checking for an equivalent non-color cue (text, checkmark, label). Tools cannot determine that a background-color is the sole carrier of meaning, nor that the selected-ring is color-only.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: Section508 and WCAG 1.4.1 cover color-only selection; Craftshift and the EAA-2025 swatch guidance note most Shopify swatch apps render unlabeled clickable divs. https://craftshift.com/shopify-european-accessibility-act-swatches/

4.1.2.platform: Ant Design Form / Form.Item
4.1.2.name: Validation error not programmatically associated with the field
4.1.2.description: Ant Design's Form renders inline validation errors visually beneath the input, but historically did not set aria-invalid on the control nor aria-describedby pointing at the error text, and labels were not always tied to inputs. The error appears in red text but is not announced when the field is focused, and the field is not exposed as invalid.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup: Please enter a valid email
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: The error text exists in the DOM, so it is visible to a scanner, but verifying that it is PROGRAMMATICALLY tied to the right input (and announced on focus / on submit) requires triggering validation and inspecting the runtime aria relationships; the visual-only error with a missing association is not reliably flagged by static rules.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: Ant Design issues #36730 (set aria-invalid/aria-describedby on invalid inputs), #28748 (link error messages to field), and #16268 ("Forms in Ant Design are not accessible"). https://github.com/ant-design/ant-design/issues/36730

4.1.2.platform: Bootstrap Modal (and hand-rolled React modals)
4.1.2.name: Background page not inert / aria-hidden focus conflict behind modal
4.1.2.description: When a Bootstrap/custom modal opens, the underlying page is not made inert and is not hidden from AT (or, conversely, aria-hidden="true" is placed on an ancestor that still contains the focused trigger). Screen-reader users can read and tab into the page behind the dialog, and focus can land on aria-hidden content, producing the "focusable element inside aria-hidden" conflict.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup: ...
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: axe flags aria-hidden containing a focusable element only when the snapshot is in that exact state; whether the background is truly inert / focus is trapped is a runtime, interaction-driven property. Confirming a SR can reach behind-modal content or that Tab escapes requires actually operating the dialog with the keyboard/AT.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: Bootstrap issue #29769 and MDN's aria-modal docs cover the inert/aria-hidden tradeoff; the focusable-inside-aria-hidden conflict is a frequent audit finding. https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/issues/29769

4.1.2.platform: MUI Autocomplete / Select (combobox)
4.1.2.name: Stale aria-activedescendant / aria-controls on closed combobox
4.1.2.description: MUI's Autocomplete leaves aria-controls pointing at a listbox id before the listbox exists, and keeps aria-activedescendant on the input set to the last-highlighted option id after the popup closes. Screen readers can announce a phantom "active" option that is no longer on screen, or reference a control that is not in the DOM, confusing combobox navigation.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup:
<input role="combobox"
  aria-expanded="false"
  aria-controls="listbox-1"        <!-- listbox not in DOM -->
  aria-activedescendant="option-7"> <!-- popup is closed -->
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: The attributes are syntactically valid (valid id references when the listbox is open), so static ARIA-attribute validity checks pass. The defect is a state/timing inconsistency between the visual popup state and the aria-* values, which only manifests during interaction and must be judged against expected combobox behavior.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: MUI issue #18133 "Some WAI-ARIA attributes are incorrect" documents aria-controls set before the listbox exists and aria-activedescendant not cleared on close. https://github.com/mui/material-ui/issues/18133

4.1.2.platform: jQuery UI / Bootstrap Tabs & Accordion
4.1.2.name: div/anchor "tab" widgets lacking tab roles and arrow-key support
4.1.2.description: Older jQuery UI and many Bootstrap-derived tab/accordion implementations render tabs as <a>/<li> or plain divs that toggle panels via click, without role="tablist"/"tab"/"tabpanel", without aria-selected/aria-controls, and without the expected arrow-key roving-tabindex behavior. Screen readers do not recognize the tab pattern and keyboard users cannot move between tabs with arrow keys.
4.1.2.typicalMarkup:
• Details
  • Reviews
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: Plain anchors with hrefs are individually valid and focusable, so structural linters see nothing wrong. Recognizing that this SHOULD be the ARIA tabs pattern (and that arrow-key navigation and aria-selected are absent) requires understanding the intended widget semantics and testing keyboard interaction.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: WAI-ARIA APG tabs pattern requires roles + arrow-key support; legacy jQuery UI / Bootstrap tab markup commonly ships without them, a recurring audit finding for interactive widgets.

4.1.2.platform: React/Vue placeholder-as-label inputs (Tailwind/MUI styled)
4.1.2.name: Placeholder used as the only label
4.1.2.description: Inputs styled by component libraries frequently use the placeholder attribute as the sole label (no <label>, no aria-label). The hint disappears once the user types, low-contrast placeholder text fails contrast, and there is no programmatic label — screen readers may announce nothing or only "edit text".
4.1.2.typicalMarkup:
<input type="email" placeholder="Email address">
<!-- no <label for>, no aria-label; placeholder is the only cue -->
4.1.2.whyAutoToolsMiss: axe reliably flags inputs with no accessible name ("Form elements must have labels"), so the bare missing-label case is automatable — flagged false. The residual judgment (is a placeholder an ADEQUATE instruction even when a label exists, contrast of the placeholder) can still need a human, but detection of no-label is a linter check.
4.1.2.realWorldNote: WCAG 3.3.2 and broad guidance treat placeholder-as-label as a failure (text vanishes on input, low contrast); extremely common in utility-CSS/component-styled forms.

4.1.3.name: Success/confirmation message injected without a live region
4.1.3.description: On submit, the form swaps in a visible 'Thank you, your message has been sent' confirmation in place of the form, but the inserted node is not a role=status / aria-live region and focus is not moved to it. Sighted users see success; screen-reader users hear nothing and may believe the submission failed and re-submit.
4.1.3.typicalMarkup: Thank you! Your message has been sent.
4.1.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: The message is valid visible text in the DOM; a static scan sees correct markup and no error. Catching it requires dynamically submitting the form AND observing (with AT or by checking for a live region / focus move) that the status change is never announced — a behavioral, human-in-the-loop check.
4.1.3.realWorldNote: Amy Carney's Squarespace audit: 'Same-page confirmation messages don't alert screen reader users of state changes' and 'error lists aren't linked to inputs or focused.' https://theamycarney.com/2024/04/02/observations-on-squarespace-accessibility/

4.1.3.name: Instant search results render with no announcement or result count
4.1.3.description: Results appear on each keystroke beneath the search box, but the results container is not a live region and the result count is never announced, so screen-reader users don't know results appeared, how many, or that the list changed. The Quick Preview is also keyboard-inaccessible and the spinner is silent.
4.1.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: Static analysis finds a labeled search input and valid result links. The absence of an announcement is a dynamic behavior that only surfaces when you type and listen with a screen reader; tools can't infer that the live update should have been announced.
4.1.3.realWorldNote: Amy Carney's Squarespace audit: 'Search results appear on keystroke but screen readers aren't notified of appearance or result count; processing spinner lacks announcements; Quick Preview not keyboard accessible.' https://theamycarney.com/2024/04/02/observations-on-squarespace-accessibility/

4.1.3.platform: Elementor Form widget / Divi Contact Form / WPForms — submission feedback
4.1.3.name: Success/error toast not in a live region; errors flagged by color only
4.1.3.description: After AJAX form submit, the success or error message is injected into a <div> that is not a live region and not focused, so screen readers never announce it. Inline validation marks invalid fields with a red border/red text only, with no programmatic error association and no text describing what's wrong or how to fix it.
4.1.3.typicalMarkup: Your message was sent!
4.1.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: The success div is valid HTML; nothing in the static DOM signals it should announce on change. Detecting that a dynamically-inserted status isn't announced requires triggering the submit and observing AT silence. Color-only error indication also needs visual judgment that no text/icon backs the red.
4.1.3.realWorldNote: ARIA live-region guidance: 'create an empty element and then update its content' — builder messages don't. https://a11y-blog.dev/en/articles/aria-live-regions/ ; matches harness 4.1.3 / 3.3.x shadow lanes.

4.1.3.platform: Shopify / WooCommerce — Add to Cart confirmation & cart drawer
4.1.3.name: Silent add-to-cart: drawer/toast update not in a live region
4.1.3.description: Clicking 'Add to cart' updates a cart-count bubble and slides open a cart drawer or shows a toast, but the success message is injected into a normal <div> with no role=status / aria-live. Sighted users see the confirmation; screen reader users get no announcement that the item was added, and focus is not moved into the drawer either.
4.1.3.typicalMarkup:
Item added to your cart

View cart (1)
4.1.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: The notification element is valid HTML with valid contrast and a labeled link, so static scanners pass it. The failure only manifests on interaction (clicking add-to-cart) and depends on whether the dynamically-shown node is in a live region AND whether focus is managed — a runtime behavior automated DOM scans don't simulate, and judging the right remediation (announce vs. move focus) is contextual.
4.1.3.realWorldNote: TestParty 'Beyond Alt Text' lists 'silent cart updates — screen reader users receive no confirmation' as a top hidden Shopify barrier; WooCommerce filed its own 4.1.3 fix for the added-to-cart message. https://testparty.ai/blog/beyond-alt-text-hidden-shopify-accessibility-barriers

4.1.3.platform: WooCommerce — store notices on page load (waitlist / coupon / stock)
4.1.3.name: Page-load notice not programmatically a status message
4.1.3.description: WooCommerce renders informational notices (e.g. 'To join the waitlist, click Notify me', coupon applied, 'only 2 left') as a styled div shown when the page renders. The notice has no role=status/alert and focus is not placed on it, so on a fresh page load it is visible but never announced to screen reader users.
4.1.3.typicalMarkup: To join the waitlist, please click the "Notify me" button.
4.1.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: There is no markup defect: contrast is fine and the text exists in the DOM. Whether a given message is a 'status message' that must be announced (vs. ordinary body copy) is a semantic judgment about its purpose and timing; axe/Lighthouse cannot infer intent and do not flag missing role=status on plain divs.
4.1.3.realWorldNote: Filed directly against WooCommerce core as a WCAG 4.1.3 failure: 'message is visually displayed, but screen readers do not announce it because it has not been programmatically defined as a status message, and focus is not set on the message when the page loads.' https://github.com/woocommerce/woocommerce/issues/59383

4.1.3.platform: Shopify / WooCommerce — AJAX filter / faceted search sidebar
4.1.3.name: Facet filtering updates grid silently; no result-count announcement
4.1.3.description: Selecting a filter checkbox (size, color, price) re-renders the product grid via AJAX with no page reload. The new result count ('24 products') and any 'No results' state are not in a live region, so screen reader users don't know the grid changed or how many products remain. Some themes also replace native checkboxes with styled divs that lose keyboard operability.
4.1.3.typicalMarkup: 24 products
4.1.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: On the initial static snapshot the markup is valid (labeled checkboxes, a count div). The defect appears only when a filter fires and content swaps without an announcement — a runtime behavior. Whether the count and no-results state qualify as status messages requiring aria-live is an intent-based judgment scanners can't make.
4.1.3.realWorldNote: Equalize Digital's FacetWP audit and Scott O'Hara's 'dynamic results' guidance cover exactly this; accessibility-test.org documents ecommerce faceted-search live-region gaps. https://equalizedigital.com/testing-facetwp-for-accessibility/ ; https://accessibility-test.org/blog/compliance/accessibility-for-e-commerce-product-filtering-and-faceted-search/

4.1.3.name: <title> and H1 never update on client-side route change
4.1.3.description: Navigating from collection to product to cart happens client-side; the document <title> stays at the homepage/store name on every route, and focus is not moved to the new page's H1. Screen reader users hear the same title on every 'page' and get no signal that navigation occurred.
4.1.3.typicalMarkup:
<head><title>Acme Store</title></head>
<!-- after client-side nav to /products/blue-shirt the title is still "Acme Store";
     no React Helmet update, no focus moved to the product <h1> -->
4.1.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: A single-page audit finds a non-empty <title> and passes 2.4.2. The failure is that the title doesn't CHANGE across virtual route transitions and is identical/non-descriptive for each view — a multi-state behavior. Tools scan one DOM state and have no concept of route changes, so they never compare titles across navigations.
4.1.3.realWorldNote: Widely documented SPA failure (Hidde Blog, Kitty Giraudel, Helsinki a11y model): SPAs keep a static <title> unless JS updates it on every route change. https://hidde.blog/accessible-page-titles-in-a-single-page-app/ ; https://saavutettavuusmalli.hel.fi/en/saavutettavuus-palvelukehityksessa/toteutus-ja-ohjelmistotestaus/single-page-applications-spas-notes-on-accessibility/

4.1.3.platform: Framer (and other React SPA exporters: Typedream, Readymag)
4.1.3.name: SPA route change leaves <title> stale and focus unmoved
4.1.3.description: Page-to-page navigation is client-side. The document <title> is not updated on route change, focus stays on the clicked link (or resets to <body>), and there is no route-change announcement. Screen-reader users get no signal a new page loaded and the title still reads the landing page.
4.1.3.typicalMarkup: Pricing
4.1.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: A single-page snapshot has a valid, non-empty <title>, so a page-load scan passes 2.4.2. The defect only appears across an in-app navigation: the scanner would need to click through routes and re-check title + focus + live announcement, which static and single-load automated tools don't do.
4.1.3.realWorldNote: Well-documented SPA failure: screen readers announce titles only on full page load and don't monitor title changes, and focus must be moved on route change — directly applicable to Framer/React-exported sites: https://medium.com/design-bootcamp/accessible-by-design-part-2-your-spa-single-page-application-is-broken-for-screen-readers-739769110ce1 and https://a11y-guidelines.orange.com/en/articles/single-page-app/

4.1.3.platform: Webflow / Bubble form success 'toast' or inline confirmation block
4.1.3.name: Submission success/error message not in a live region
4.1.3.description: After form submit, Webflow swaps in its success div (or Bubble shows an alert element) by toggling display, but the message is not a status/live region. Sighted users see 'Thanks, we got it!' or an error banner; screen-reader users get no announcement that submission succeeded or failed.
4.1.3.typicalMarkup:
Thank you! Your submission has been received!
Something went wrong
4.1.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: The success/fail divs exist in the DOM at page load with display:none and no role=status / aria-live, which is valid markup. A static scan can't know that toggling display later is a 'status message' that should be announced; verifying the absence of an announcement requires submitting the form with a screen reader running.
4.1.3.realWorldNote: Webflow's default form success/fail blocks have no live region; accessible practice is role=status/aria-live for submission feedback (4.1.3). Background: https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/notifications/ and toast/live-region gap discussion: https://a11y-blog.dev/en/articles/aria-live-regions/

4.1.3.platform: React Router / Vue Router / Angular Router SPA
4.1.3.name: No focus reset or route announcement on navigation
4.1.3.description: After a client-side route change the new view is rendered but keyboard focus stays on the link that was clicked (or is lost to <body>) and nothing is announced via a live region. A screen-reader user hears no indication that navigation occurred; a keyboard user must tab from wherever focus was stranded. There is no route-announcer and focus is not moved to the new page heading.
4.1.3.typicalMarkup:
Pricing

Pricing

...
4.1.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: Focus location after a JS navigation and the presence/firing of a route-announcer live region are runtime behaviors triggered by user interaction. Static and single-snapshot scanners do not perform the navigation and observe where focus lands or whether anything was announced, so they report nothing.
4.1.3.realWorldNote: react-router discussion #9863 and the long-running issue #5210 ("focus not reset when route changed") document this; James Shakespeare and TestParty both prescribe moving focus to an autofocusing h1. https://github.com/remix-run/react-router/discussions/9863

4.1.3.name: Toast/snackbar not in a live region — never announced
4.1.3.description: MUI Snackbar renders transient feedback ("Item saved", "Network error") but in many real integrations it is not wired as a status/alert live region (role/aria-live missing, or the message mounts then the region's content is replaced rather than added). The toast appears and auto-dismisses purely visually; screen-reader users never learn the action's outcome. Nesting (snackbar fired from inside a dialog or menu) makes the skip even worse.
4.1.3.typicalMarkup: Item saved
4.1.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: The element only exists for a few seconds after a user action and may be gone before/at the moment of scan. Whether a polite/assertive region actually announced depends on AT behavior and on the timing/insertion method, which a DOM linter cannot evaluate. axe will not flag a plain div with text as a 4.1.3 failure.
4.1.3.realWorldNote: MUI issue #29080 "Snackbars not read by screen reader" and #30097 (snackbar from a button inside a dialog not read); maintainers/community note toasts are often not implemented as live regions. https://github.com/mui/material-ui/issues/29080

4.1.3.platform: React conditionally-rendered form error summary / aria-live status
4.1.3.name: Submit-time errors rendered but not announced; focus not moved
4.1.3.description: On form submit, a React app conditionally renders an error summary or per-field messages into the DOM, but the container is not a live region and focus is not moved to it. Sighted users see red errors; screen-reader users get no announcement and remain focused on the submit button, unaware the submission failed.
4.1.3.whyAutoToolsMiss: The error text is present in the post-submit DOM, so a snapshot scan sees content, not a failure. Whether it was ANNOUNCED (live region) or focus was moved to it is a dynamic, interaction-and-timing property invisible to static/single-snapshot tools.
4.1.3.realWorldNote: TetraLogical and Up Your A11y describe accessible error-summary patterns requiring focus management or a live region; conditionally-rendered React errors routinely omit both. https://tetralogical.com/blog/2024/10/21/foundations-form-validation-and-error-messages/
